arXiv:1506.06377v2 [quant-ph] 13 Aug 2015

Measures of quantum correlations in infinite-dimensional systems

M.E. Shirokov Note: Steklov Mathematical Institute, RAS, Moscow, email:msh@mi.ras.ru
Abstract

Several important measures of quantum correlations of a state of a finite-dimensional composite system are defined as linear combinations of marginal entropies of this state. This paper is devoted to the infinite-dimensional generalizations of such quantities and to the analysis of their properties.

We introduce the notion of faithful extension of a linear combination of marginal entropies and consider several concrete examples starting with the quantum mutual information and the quantum conditional entropy.

Then we show that the conditional mutual information can be uniquely defined as a lower semicontinuous function on the set of all states of a tripartite infinite-dimensional system possessing all the basic properties valid in finite dimensions.

Infinite-dimensional generalizations of some other measures of quantum correlations in multipartite quantum systems are also considered. It is shown that almost all of these generalized measures are globally lower semicontinuous and possess local continuity properties which essentially simplify their use in analysis of quantum systems.

In the second part of the paper we consider applications of the general results of its first part, in particular, to the theory of infinite-dimensional quantum channels and their capacities. We also show the existence of the Fawzi-Renner recovery channel reproducing marginal states for all tripartite states (including states with infinite marginal entropies) starting with the corresponding finite-dimensional result.

1 Introduction

Characterization of quantum correlations in composite quantum systems is one of the main problems in quantum information theory which attracted attention from the middle of 20-th century. A notable progress in this direction had been achieved during the last two decades when several quantities characterizing special forms of quantum correlations had been found and explored. It is natural that initially all these characteristics were studied in finite-dimensional settings to avoid analytical problems arising in dealing with infinite-dimensional quantum systems (such as discontinuity and infinite values of the von Neumann entropy, noncompactness of a state space, etc.) Nevertheless, keeping in mind the physical applications it seems reasonable to construct infinite-dimensional generalizations of the commonly used information quantities and to study their properties.

One of the main problems in infinite-dimensional generalization of information quantities is the appearance of the uncertainty "​∞−∞​""\infty-\infty" in their original definitions. For example, many important characteristics of a state ω\omega of a multipartite finite-dimensional system A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n} are defined as a real linear combination of the marginal entropies

∑kαk​H​(ωXk),\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}), (1)

where ωXk\omega_{X_{k}} is a partial state of ω\omega corresponding to a subsystem XkX_{k} of A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n}. Linear combination (1) correctly determines a value in [−∞,+∞][-\infty,+\infty] only for states ω\omega of an infinite-dimensional system A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n} for which all the summands in (1) are either >−∞>-\infty or <+∞<+\infty. Since the states with finite von Neumann entropy form a first category subset within the set of all states [40], a direct translation of definition (1) to the case of infinite-dimensional multipartite systems makes the corresponding quantity undefined for ”almost all” states.

Fortunately, the above problem can be (partially or completely) solved by using alternative expressions for (1) consisting of terms which are more stable under passage to infinite dimensions. The simplest example is using the expression

H(ωA​B∥ωA⊗ωB),H(\omega_{AB}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B}), (2)

where H(⋅∥⋅)H(\cdot\|\cdot) is the quantum relative entropy, instead of the linear combination

H⁡(ωA)+H⁡(ωB)−H⁡(ωA​B)H(\omega_{A})+H(\omega_{B})-H(\omega_{AB}) (3)

defining quantum mutual information of a state ωA​B\omega_{AB} of a finite-dimensional bipartite system. Properties of the relative entropy show that (2) gives adequate definition of the quantum mutual information for any state ωA​B\omega_{AB} of infinite-dimensional bipartite system inheriting all basic properties of this quantity (nonnegativity, monotonicity, etc, see Sec. 4.1).

Motivated by the coincidence of (2) and (3) the quantum conditional entropy H​(A|B)ω=H⁡(ωA​B)−H⁡(ωB)\,H(A|B)_{\omega}=H(\omega_{AB})-H(\omega_{B})\, is extended in [27] to the convex set {ωA​B|H⁡(ωA)<+∞}\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{AB}\,|\,H(\omega_{A})<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\} (containing states with H⁡(ωA​B)=H⁡(ωB)=+∞H(\omega_{AB})=H(\omega_{B})=+\infty) by the formula

H(A|B)ω=H(ωA)−H(ωA​B∥ωA⊗ωB)H(A|B)_{\omega}=H(\omega_{A})-H(\omega_{AB}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B}) (4)

preserving all basic properties of the quantum conditional entropy (monotonicity, concavity, subadditivity). This extension has several important applications (see Section 5).

In the first part of this paper we begin with introducing the notion of a faithful extension (𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension) of linear combination (1) as an extension satisfying the particular ”robustness” requirement (Def.3), which seems reasonable from the both analytical and physical points of view.

Then we consider infinite-dimensional generalizations of several entropic quantities having form (1), starting with the analysis of continuity properties of the quantum mutual information I​(A:B)ωI(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} defined by formula (2) as a function of ω\omega (Theorem 4.1). Then we describe extension (4) of the quantum conditional entropy and its applications.

Special attention is paid to generalization of the conditional mutual information

I(A:C|B)ω=H(ωA​B)+H(ωB​C)−H(ωA​B​C)−H(ωB)I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=H(\omega_{AB})+H(\omega_{BC})-H(\omega_{ABC})-H(\omega_{B})

having in mind its numerous applications. It is shown that I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} has an unique lower semicontinuous extension to the whole set of states of an infinite-dimensional tripartite system A​B​CABC possessing all the basic properties of the conditional mutual information valid in finite dimensions (Theorem 6.1).

Infinite-dimensional generalizations of some other measures of quantum correlations in multipartite systems (topological entanglement entropy, unconditional and conditional secrecy monotone SnS_{n}, etc.) are also considered.

In the study of measures of quantum correlations we pay special attention to their continuity properties. In finite dimensions any quantity (1) is obviously continuous on the whole set of states.11 1 There exist discontinuous measures of quantum correlations in finite-dimensional multipartite systems and their discontinuity has a physical meaning. Such measure (called irreducible three-party correlation) is considered in [8, 35]. Its discontinuity is a corollary of the discontinuity of the maximal entropy inference – an interesting purely quantum effect discovered by Knauf and Weis [24]. In infinite dimensions global continuity is a very strong requirement, but one can try to obtain conditions for local continuity, i.e. continuity with respect to variation of a states within a particular subset. Intuitively, local continuity of some measure of quantum correlations can be understood as stability with respect to local perturbations of a state (which are unavoidable due to finite accuracy of the state preparation procedure).

It turns out that for all commonly used quantum correlation measures (defined by formula (1) in finite dimensions) there exist simple sufficient conditions for local continuity expressed via local continuity of one or several marginal entropies (not necessarily involved in (1)). These conditions look especially surprising when local continuity of only one marginal entropy implies local continuity of the whole linear combination (1) consisting of nn summands (see, for instance, Proposition 7.1).

We also obtain general results concerning preserving local continuity under conditioning and partial trace (Proposition 4.3 and Corollary 5).

In the second part of the paper we consider applications of the general results of its first part to the theory of infinite-dimensional quantum channels and their capacities. In particular, we show that the classical entanglement-assisted capacity with the constraint defined by the linear inequality Tr​F​ρ≤E\mathrm{Tr}F\rho\leq E is continuous on the set of all channels equipped with the strong convergence topology provided the von Neumann entropy is continuous on the set of states satisfying this inequality (Proposition 8.3).

By using the extended conditional mutual information we show the existence of the Fawzi-Renner recovery channel exactly reproducing marginal states for all tripartite states (including states with infinite marginal entropies) starting with the corresponding finite-dimensional result from [11] (Proposition 8.4).

2 Preliminaries

Let ℋ\mathcal{H} be a separable Hilbert space, 𝔅⁡(ℋ)\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}) and 𝔗⁡(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}) – Banach spaces of all bounded operators and of all trace-class operators in ℋ\mathcal{H}, 𝔗+​(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}) – the cone of positive operators in 𝔗⁡(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}), 𝔖⁡(ℋ)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}) – the set of quantum states (operators in 𝔗+​(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}) with unit trace) [16, 33].

Trace class operators (not only states) will be denoted by the Greek letters ρ\rho, σ\sigma, ω\omega, … All others linear operators (in particular, unbounded operators) will be denoted by the Latin letters AA, BB, FF, HH, …

Denote by IℋI_{\mathcal{H}} the unit operator in a Hilbert space ℋ\mathcal{H} and by Idℋ\mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal{\mathcal{H}}} the identity transformation of the Banach space 𝔗⁡(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}).

A quantum operation Φ\,\Phi from a system AA to a system BB is a completely positive trace non-increasing linear map 𝔗⁡(ℋA)→𝔗⁡(ℋB)\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{A})\rightarrow\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{B}), where ℋA\mathcal{H}_{A} and ℋB\mathcal{H}_{B} are Hilbert spaces associated with the systems AA and BB. A trace preserving quantum operation is called quantum channel [16, 33].

The von Neumann entropy H⁡(ρ)=Tr​η​(ρ)H(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}\eta(\rho) of a state ρ∈𝔖⁡(ℋ)\rho\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}), where η⁡(x)=−x​log⁡x\eta(x)=-x\log x, has the natural extension to the cone 𝔗+​(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}) (cf.[31])22 2 Here and in what follows log\log denotes the natural logarithm.

H⁡(ρ)=Tr​ρ​H​(ρTr​ρ)=Tr​η​(ρ)−η⁡(Tr​ρ),ρ∈𝔗+​(ℋ).H(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}\rho H\!\left(\frac{\rho}{\mathrm{Tr}\rho}\right)=\mathrm{Tr}\eta(\rho)-\eta(\mathrm{Tr}\rho),\quad\rho\in\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}). (5)

Nonnegativity, concavity and lower semicontinuity of the von Neumann entropy on the cone 𝔗+​(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}) follow from the corresponding properties of this function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋ)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}) [31, 40]. By definition

H⁡(λ​ρ)=λ​H​(ρ),λ≥0.H(\lambda\rho)=\lambda H(\rho),\quad\lambda\geq 0. (6)

The concavity of the von Neumann entropy is supplemented by the inequality

H⁡(λ​ρ+(1−λ)​σ)≤λ​H​(ρ)+(1−λ)​H​(σ)+max⁡{Tr​ρ,Tr​σ}​h2​(λ),H\left(\lambda\rho+(1-\lambda)\sigma\right)\leq\lambda H(\rho)+(1-\lambda)H(\sigma)+\max\{\mathrm{Tr}\rho,\mathrm{Tr}\sigma\}\hskip 1.0pth_{2}(\lambda), (7)

where h2​(λ)=η⁡(λ)+η⁡(1−λ)h_{2}(\lambda)=\eta(\lambda)+\eta(1-\lambda), valid for any operators ρ,σ∈𝔗+​(ℋ)\rho,\sigma\in\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}).

The quantum relative entropy for two operators ρ\rho and σ\sigma in 𝔗+​(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}) is defined as follows (cf.[31])

H(ρ∥σ)=∑i=1+∞⟨i|ρlogρ−ρlogσ+σ−ρ|i⟩,H(\rho\,\|\hskip 1.0pt\sigma)=\sum_{i=1}^{+\infty}\langle i|\,\rho\log\rho-\rho\log\sigma+\sigma-\rho\,|i\rangle,

where {|i⟩}i=1+∞\{|i\rangle\}_{i=1}^{+\infty} is the orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of the operator ρ\rho and it is assumed that H(ρ∥σ)=+∞H(\rho\,\|\sigma)=+\infty if supp​ρ\,\mathrm{supp}\rho is not contained in supp​σ\mathrm{supp}\hskip 1.0pt\sigma. This definition implies

H(λρ∥λσ)=λH(ρ∥σ),λ≥0.H(\lambda\rho\,\|\hskip 1.0pt\lambda\sigma)=\lambda H(\rho\,\|\hskip 1.0pt\sigma),\quad\lambda\geq 0. (8)

We will use the following result of the purification theory.

Lemma 1. Let ℋ\mathcal{H} and 𝒦\mathcal{K} be Hilbert spaces such that dimℋ=dim𝒦\,\dim\mathcal{H}=\dim\mathcal{K}. For an arbitrary pure state ω0\omega_{0} in 𝔖⁡(ℋ⊗𝒦)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}\otimes\mathcal{K}) and an arbitrary sequence {ρk}\{\rho_{k}\} of states in 𝔖⁡(ℋ)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}) converging to the state ρ0=Tr𝒦​ω0\rho_{0}=\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathcal{K}}\omega_{0} there exists a sequence {ωk}\{\omega_{k}\} of pure states in 𝔖⁡(ℋ⊗𝒦)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}\otimes\mathcal{K}) converging to the state ω0\omega_{0} such thatρk=Tr𝒦​ωk\rho_{k}=\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathcal{K}}\omega_{k} for all k\,k.

The assertion of Lemma 2 can be proved by noting that the infimum in the definition of the Bures distance (or the supremum in the definition of the Uhlmann fidelity) between two quantum states can be taken only over all purifications of one state with fixed purification of the another state and that the convergence of a sequence of states in the trace norm distance implies its convergence in the Bures distance [11, 16, 33].

We will use the following property of the von Neumann entropy.

Lemma 2. Let ωA1​…​An\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}} be a state of n\,n-partite system A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n} and {PA1k}k⊂𝔅⁡(ℋA1)\{P^{k}_{A_{1}}\}_{k}\subset\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}}),…, {PAnk}k⊂𝔅⁡(ℋAn)\{P^{k}_{A_{n}}\}_{k}\subset\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{n}}) sequences of projectors strongly converging to the identity operators IA1I_{A_{1}},…,IAnI_{A_{n}}. Let ωA1​…​Ank=λk−1​Qk​ωA1​…​An​Qk\;\omega^{k}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}=\lambda_{k}^{-1}Q_{k}\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}Q_{k}, where Qk=PA1k⊗…⊗PAnkQ_{k}=P^{k}_{A_{1}}\otimes\ldots\otimes P^{k}_{A_{n}}, λk=Tr​Qk​ωA1​…​An\lambda_{k}=\mathrm{Tr}Q_{k}\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}} and Ai1​…​Aim\,A_{i_{1}}...A_{i_{m}}, m≤nm\leq n, be a subsystem of A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n}. Then

limk→∞H⁡(ωAi1​…​Aimk)=H⁡(ωAi1​…​Aim)≤+∞.\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(\omega^{k}_{A_{i_{1}}\ldots A_{i_{m}}})=H(\omega_{A_{i_{1}}\ldots A_{i_{m}}})\leq+\infty.

Proof. By noting that

λk​ωAi1​…​Aimk≤PAi1k⊗…⊗PAimk​ωAi1​…​Aim​PAi1k⊗…⊗PAimk∀k,\lambda_{k}\omega^{k}_{A_{i_{1}}...A_{i_{m}}}\leq P^{k}_{A_{i_{1}}}\otimes...\otimes P^{k}_{A_{i_{m}}}\,\omega_{A_{i_{1}}...A_{i_{m}}}\,P^{k}_{A_{i_{1}}}\otimes...\otimes P^{k}_{A_{i_{m}}}\quad\forall k,

this assertion can be proved by using Simon’s convergence theorems for the von Neumann entropy [30, the Appendix].□\square

Remark 1. Throughout the paper we will consider that continuous functions on a metric space are finite on this space (in contrast to lower (upper) semicontinuous functions which can take infinite values). We will say that local continuity of a function ff implies local continuity of a function gg\hskip 1.0pt if

limk→∞f⁡(xk)=f⁡(x0)≠±∞⇒limk→∞g⁡(xk)=g⁡(x0)≠±∞\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}f(x_{k})=f(x_{0})\neq\pm\infty\quad\Rightarrow\quad\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}g(x_{k})=g(x_{0})\neq\pm\infty

for any sequence {xk}\{x_{k}\} converging to x0x_{0}.

We will refer to the following simple fact.

Lemma 3. Let f1,…​fnf_{1},...f_{n} be nonnegative lower semicontinuous functions on a metric space XX. Then local continuity of ∑k=1nfk\,\sum_{k=1}^{n}f_{k} implies local continuity of all the functions f1,…​fnf_{1},...f_{n}.

Remark 2. Throughout the paper we will assume that any function FF on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋ)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}) of quantum states is extended to the cone 𝔗+​(ℋ)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}) by the formula

F⁡(ρ)=[Tr​ρ]​F​(ρTr​ρ)F(\rho)=[\mathrm{Tr}\rho]F\left(\frac{\rho}{\mathrm{Tr}\rho}\right)

Note that such extension of a function F⁡(ρ)=∑kαk​H​(Φk​(ρ))F(\rho)=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\Phi_{k}(\rho)), where Φk\Phi_{k} are positive linear maps, is determined by the same formula provided that extension (5) of the von Neumann entropy is used.

3 On faithful extension of entropic quantities

Quantum correlations of a state of a finite-dimensional nn-partite system A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n} are described by different entropic quantities (such as quantum mutual information, quantum conditional entropy, conditional mutual information, topological entanglement entropy, etc.), defined as a real linear combination of marginal entropies, i.e. as a function

F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαk​H​(ωXk)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}) (9)

on the set of all states of the system, where ωXk\omega_{X_{k}} is a partial state of ωA1​…​An\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}} corresponding to a subsystem XkX_{k} of A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n}.

In infinite dimensions such entropic quantity is correctly defined if all the marginal entropies H⁡(ωXk)\,H(\omega_{X_{k}})\, involved in the corresponding linear combination (9) are finite (or at least this linear combination does not contain the uncertainty "​∞−∞​""\infty-\infty"). Nevertheless such narrow domain of definition can be extended by using althernative expressions, which are more stable under passage to infinite dimensions than the linear combination in (9). Examples of such extensions for quantum mutual information and for quantum conditional entropy have been mentioned in the Introduction.

These examples motivate questions about possible extensions of linear combination (9) to states at which it is not correctly defined and about requirements to these extensions in general settings.

In general the function FF in (9) is not lower or upper semicontinuous on the set of states at which it is well defined (the linear combination does not contain the uncertainty "​∞−∞​""\infty-\infty"), but Lemma 2 shows that for any such state this function possesses the following property:

limk→∞F⁡(ωA1​…​Ank)=F⁡(ωA1​…​An)∈[−∞,+∞]\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}F(\omega^{k}_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})\in[-\infty,+\infty] (10)

for any sequence of ”truncated” states

ωA1​…​Ank=λk−1​Qk​ωA1​…​An​Qk,Qk=PA1k⊗…⊗PAnk,λk=Tr​Qk​ωA1​…​An,\omega^{k}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}=\lambda_{k}^{-1}Q_{k}\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}Q_{k},\quad Q_{k}=P^{k}_{A_{1}}\otimes\ldots\otimes P^{k}_{A_{n}},\;\lambda_{k}=\mathrm{Tr}Q_{k}\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}},

determined by sequences {PA1k}k⊂𝔅⁡(ℋA1)\{P^{k}_{A_{1}}\}_{k}\subset\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}}),…, {PAnk}k⊂𝔅⁡(ℋAn)\{P^{k}_{A_{n}}\}_{k}\subset\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{n}}) of projectors strongly converging to the identity operators IA1I_{A_{1}},…,IAnI_{A_{n}}.33 3 If F⁡(ωA1​…​An)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) is well defined then F⁡(ωA1​…​Ank)F(\omega^{k}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) is well defined for all kk (since finiteness of H⁡(ρ)H(\rho) implies finiteness of H⁡(P​ρ​P)H(P\rho P) for any projector PP).

This property can be treated as a self-consistency or stability of FF with respect to state truncation. It seems to be a reasonable requirement for any measure of quantum correlations from the both analytical and physical points of view. This motivates the following definition.

Definition 1. Let 𝒜\mathcal{A} be a subset of states of a multipartite system A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n} such that

ωA1​…​An∈𝒜⇒[Tr​Q​ωA1​…​An]−1​Q​ωA1​…​An​Q∈𝒜,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\in\mathcal{A}\quad\Rightarrow\quad[\mathrm{Tr}Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}]^{-1}Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}Q\in\mathcal{A}, (11)

where Q=PA1⊗…⊗PAnQ=P_{A_{1}}\otimes\ldots\otimes P_{A_{n}}, for any projectors PAi∈𝔅⁡(ℋAi)P_{A_{i}}\in\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{i}}), i=1,n¯i=\overline{1,n}. We will say that a function FF taking values in [−∞,+∞][-\infty,+\infty] is faithful on 𝒜\mathcal{A} if for any state ωA1​…​An∈𝒜\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\in\mathcal{A} the above condition (10) is valid.

It is clear that continuity of FF implies faithfulness of FF, but the reverse is not true. The simplest example is given by the von Neumann entropy of a marginal state F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=H⁡(ωX)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=H(\omega_{X}), X⊆A1​…​AnX\subseteq A_{1}...A_{n}, which is a faithful function on the whole set of states of A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n} by Lemma 2.

The faithfulness property seems to be a reasonable replacement for the continuity in infinite dimensions. Many characteristics of states of bi- and multipartite infinite-dimensional systems are globally faithful but not continuous. For example, the bi- and multipartite quantum mutual information, the Entanglement of Formation of a bipartite state (defined as a ”continuous” convex roof, see [37]), etc. The faithfulness of these characteristics follows from their lower semicontinuity and monotonicity under local operations.

Lemma 4. If FF is a lower semicontinuous function on a subset 𝒜\mathcal{A} of 𝔗+​(ℋA1​…​An)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) satisfying condition (11) and F⁡(Φ1⊗…⊗Φn​(ω))≤F⁡(ω)F(\Phi_{1}\otimes...\otimes\Phi_{n}(\omega))\leq F(\omega) for any ω∈𝒜\,\omega\in\mathcal{A} and arbitrary quantum operations Φ1:A1→A1,..,Φn:An→An\,\Phi_{1}\!:A_{1}\rightarrow\!A_{1},..,\Phi_{n}\!:A_{n}\rightarrow\!A_{n} then FF is faithful on 𝒜∩𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\mathcal{A}\cap\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}).

The faithfulness is a very convenient property from the analytical point of view. It is the faithfulness of the bipartite quantum mutual information that was implicitly used in [27] to prove concavity and other basic properties of quantum conditional entropy for its extension (4).

The above arguments show that a function F^\widehat{F} can be treated as an adequate extension of a particular information quantity FF to a subset 𝒜\mathcal{A} of 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) if it is faithful on this subset.

Definition 2. A function F^\widehat{F} is called faithful extension (briefly, 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension) of the function FF in (9) to a subset 𝒜∈𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\mathcal{A}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) satisfying condition (11) if it is faithful on 𝒜\mathcal{A} and F^​(ω)=F​(ω)\widehat{F}(\omega)=F(\omega) for any state ω∈𝒜\omega\in\mathcal{A} for which F⁡(ω)F(\omega) is well defined.

Definition 3 implies the following simple observations used below.

Lemma 5. If 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of a linear combination of marginal entropies to a particular subset exists then it is uniquely defined.

Lemma 6. If F^1\widehat{F}_{1} and F^2\widehat{F}_{2} are 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extensions of quantities F1F_{1} and F2F_{2} to a particular set 𝒜\mathcal{A} such that c1​F^1+c2​F^2c_{1}\widehat{F}_{1}+c_{2}\widehat{F}_{2}, c1,c2∈ℝc_{1},c_{2}\in\mathbb{R}, is well defined on 𝒜\mathcal{A} then c1​F^1+c2​F^2c_{1}\widehat{F}_{1}+c_{2}\widehat{F}_{2} is a 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of the quantity c1​F1+c2​F2c_{1}F_{1}+c_{2}F_{2} to the set 𝒜\mathcal{A}.

We finish this section by a general result concerning the case when linear combination (9) is bounded on the set where it is well defined.44 4 Examples corresponding to this case are considered below (see Corollaries 4.1,5,6.1,7.1). This result (proved by Winter’s modification of the Alicki-Fannes technic [3, 43]) shows that boundedness of (9) implies its uniform continuity and gives estimates for its variation.

Proposition 1. If a function F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαk​H​(ωXk)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}) is bounded on the set 𝔖f={ωA1​…​An|maxi⁡rank​ωAi<+∞}\;\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}}=\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\hskip 1.0pt|\hskip 1.0pt\max_{i}\mathrm{rank}\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{i}}<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\} then it has a unique continuous extension F^\widehat{F} to the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) such that

|F^​(ω1)−F^​(ω2)|≤ε​supω,ω′∈𝔖f|F⁡(ω)−F⁡(ω′)|+(1+ε)​h2​(ε1+ε)​∑k|αk|\!|\widehat{F}(\omega^{1})-\widehat{F}(\omega^{2})|\leq\,\varepsilon\sup_{\omega,\omega^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}}}|F(\omega)-F(\omega^{\prime})|+(1+\varepsilon)h_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right)\sum_{k}|\alpha_{k}| (12)

for any ω1,ω2∈𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\,\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) such that ε=12​‖ω1−ω2‖1<1\;\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{1}-\omega^{2}\|_{1}<1\,, where h2​(⋅)\,h_{2}(\cdot)\, is the binary entropy.

If F\,F is a concave (corresp., convex) function on 𝔖f\,\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}} then F^\,\widehat{F} is a concave (corresp., convex) function on 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) and ∑k|αk|\,\sum_{k}|\alpha_{k}| in (12) can be replaced by ∑k:αk>0|αk|\,\sum_{k:\alpha_{k}>0}|\alpha_{k}| (corresp., by ∑k:αk<0|αk|\,\sum_{k:\alpha_{k}<0}|\alpha_{k}|).

Proof. It suffices to show that (12) holds with F^=F\widehat{F}=F for any states ω1,ω2∈𝔖f\,\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}}, since this would imply that FF is a uniformly continuous function on the dense subset 𝔖f\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}} of 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) uniquely extended, by a standard way, to a continuous function F^\widehat{F} on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) satisfying (12).

The concavity of the von Neumann entropy and inequality (7) imply

λ​F​(ω1)+(1−λ)​F​(ω2)+C−​h2​(λ)≤F⁡(λ​ω1+(1−λ)​ω2)≤λ​F​(ω1)+(1−λ)​F​(ω2)+C+​h2​(λ)\begin{array}[]{cc}\lambda F\left(\omega^{1}\right)+(1-\lambda)F\left(\omega^{2}\right)+C_{-}h_{2}(\lambda)\\ \\ \leq F\left(\lambda\omega^{1}+(1-\lambda)\omega^{2}\right)\leq\\ \\ \lambda F\left(\omega^{1}\right)+(1-\lambda)F\left(\omega^{2}\right)+C_{+}h_{2}(\lambda)\end{array} (13)

for any states ω1,ω2∈𝔖f\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}}, where C−=∑k:αk<0αk\,C_{-}=\sum_{k:\alpha_{k}<0}\alpha_{k}\, and C+=∑k:αk>0αk\,C_{+}=\sum_{k:\alpha_{k}>0}\alpha_{k}.

Following [43] introduce the state ω∗=(1+ε)−1​(ω1+[ω2−ω1]+)\,\omega^{*}=(1+\varepsilon)^{-1}(\omega^{1}+[\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{2}-\omega^{1}]_{+}). Then

11+ε​ω1+ε1+ε​ω~1=ω∗=11+ε​ω2+ε1+ε​ω~2,\frac{1}{1+\varepsilon}\,\omega^{1}+\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\,\tilde{\omega}^{1}=\omega^{*}=\frac{1}{1+\varepsilon}\,\omega^{2}+\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\,\tilde{\omega}^{2}, (14)

where ω~1=ε−1​[ω2−ω1]+\,\tilde{\omega}^{1}=\varepsilon^{-1}[\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{2}-\omega^{1}]_{+}\, and ω~2=ε−1​((1+ε)​ω∗−ω2)\,\tilde{\omega}^{2}=\varepsilon^{-1}((1+\varepsilon)\omega^{*}-\omega^{2}) are states in 𝔖f\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}}. By applying (13) to the above convex decompositions of ω∗\,\omega^{*} we obtain

11+ε​(F⁡(ω1)−F⁡(ω2))≤ε1+ε​(F⁡(ω~2)−F⁡(ω~1))+(C+−C−)​h2​(ε1+ε)\frac{1}{1+\varepsilon}\,(F(\omega^{1})-F(\omega^{2}))\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\,(F(\tilde{\omega}^{2})-F(\tilde{\omega}^{1}))+(C_{+}-C_{-})\hskip 1.0pth_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right)

and

11+ε​(F⁡(ω2)−F⁡(ω1))≤ε1+ε​(F⁡(ω~1)−F⁡(ω~2))+(C+−C−)​h2​(ε1+ε).\frac{1}{1+\varepsilon}\,(F(\omega^{2})-F(\omega^{1}))\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\,(F(\tilde{\omega}^{1})-F(\tilde{\omega}^{2}))+(C_{+}-C_{-})\hskip 1.0pth_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right).

These inequalities imply (12) with F^=F\widehat{F}=F, since C+−C−=∑k|αk|\,C_{+}-C_{-}=\sum_{k}|\alpha_{k}|.

The last assertion of the proposition follows from the above proof. □\;\square

If dA≐dimℋA<+∞\,d_{A}\doteq\dim\mathcal{H}_{A}<+\infty\, then Proposition 3 imply the following continuity bounds for the von Neumann entropy and for the conditional entropy

|H⁡(ω1)−H⁡(ω2)|≤ε​log⁡dA+(1+ε)​h2​(ε1+ε)|H(\omega^{1})-H(\omega^{2})|\leq\,\varepsilon\log d_{A}+(1+\varepsilon)h_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right) (15)

and

|H​(A|B)ω1−H​(A|B)ω2|≤2​ε​log⁡dA+(1+ε)​h2​(ε1+ε)|H(A|B)_{\omega^{1}}-H(A|B)_{\omega^{2}}|\leq 2\varepsilon\log d_{A}+(1+\varepsilon)h_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right) (16)

(the concavity of the both these quantities was taken into account).

Continuity bound (15) is close (and asymptotically equivalent) to the sharpest continuity bound for the von Neumann entropy

|H⁡(ω1)−H⁡(ω2)|≤ε​log⁡(dA−1)+h2​(ε)|H(\omega^{1})-H(\omega^{2})|\leq\varepsilon\log(d_{A}-1)+h_{2}(\varepsilon)

obtained by Audenaert [4]. Continuity bound (16) coincides with the tight continuity bound for the conditional entropy proved by Winter using (14) and the special representation for the conditional entropy [43, Lemma 2]. So, we have some reasons to expect that Proposition 3 gives quite sharp continuity bounds despite its universality.

4 Quantum mutual information and its use

4.1 Bipartite case

Quantum correlations of a state ωA​B\,\omega_{AB}\, of a finite-dimensional bipartite quantum system A​BAB are characterized by the value

I​(A:B)ω=H⁡(ωA)+H⁡(ωB)−H⁡(ωA​B)I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}=H(\omega_{A})+H(\omega_{B})-H(\omega_{AB}) (17)

called quantum mutual information of this state [29, 33, 39].

In infinite dimensions the linear combination of marginal entropies in (17) may contain the uncertainty "​∞−∞​""\infty-\infty", but it can be correctly defined for any state ωA​B\omega_{AB} (as a value in [0,+∞][0,+\infty]) by the expression

I(A:B)ω=H(ωA​B∥ωA⊗ωB)I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}=H(\omega_{AB}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B}) (18)

coinciding with (17) for any state ωA​B\omega_{AB} with finite marginal entropies.

In infinite dimensions the right hand side of (18) plays a role of ”building block” in construction of many characteristics of quantum systems and channels. It is used in extension (4) of quantum conditional entropy, in the definitions of quantum mutual and coherent informations of an infinite-dimensional quantum channel (see Sect.8.1,8.2 below), etc.

In some applications quantity (17) is used with arbitrarily positive trace class operators ωA​B\omega_{AB} (not only states). In this case (6) and (8) imply

I(A:B)ω=H(ωA​B∥ωA⊗ωBTr​ωA​B).I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}=H\left(\omega_{AB}\,\|\;\frac{\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B}}{\mathrm{Tr}\omega_{AB}}\right).

Basic properties of the relative entropy show that ω↦I​(A:B)ω\omega\mapsto I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} is a lower semicontinuous function on the cone 𝔗+​(ℋA​B)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) possessing the following properties:

  1. A1)

    I​(A:B)ω≥0I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}\geq 0 for any operator ωA​B\omega_{AB} and I​(A:B)ω=0I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}=0 if and only if ωA​B\omega_{AB} is a product operator, i.e. [Tr​ωA​B]​ωA​B=ωA⊗ωB[\mathrm{Tr}\omega_{AB}]\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{AB}=\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B};

  2. A2)

    monotonicity under local reduction: I​(A:B​C)ω≥I​(A:B)ωI(A\!:\!BC)_{\omega}\geq I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega};

  3. A3)

    monotonicity under local operations: I​(A:B)ω≥I​(A′:B′)ΦA⊗ΦB​(ω)I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}\geq I(A^{\prime}\!:\!B^{\prime})_{\Phi_{\!A}\otimes\Phi_{B}(\omega)} for arbitrary quantum operations ΦA:A→A′\Phi_{A}:A\rightarrow A^{\prime} and ΦB:B→B′\Phi_{B}:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}; 55 5 If ΦA\Phi_{A} and ΦB\Phi_{B} are quantum channels then this property directly follows from the monotonicity of the relative entropy, if ΦA\Phi_{A} and ΦB\Phi_{B} are trace-non-preserving quantum operations then additional arguments are required, for example, formula (91) in the Appendix can be used.

  4. A4)

    additivity: I​(A​A′:B​B′)ω⊗ω′=I​(A:B)ω+I​(A′:B′)ω′I(AA^{\prime}\!:\!BB^{\prime})_{\omega\otimes\omega^{\prime}}=I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}+I(A^{\prime}\!:\!B^{\prime})_{\omega^{\prime}}.

By Lemma 3 the lower semicontinuity of I​(A:B)ωI(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} and property A3 show that I​(A:B)ωI(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} defined by (18) is the 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of (17) to the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA​B)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}).

We will use the following upper bound

I​(A:B)ω≤2​min⁡{H⁡(ωA),H⁡(ωB)}I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}\leq 2\min\{H(\omega_{A}),H(\omega_{B})\} (19)

mentioned in [29]. It directly follows from identity (88) in the Appendix.

The following theorem gives local continuity conditions for the bipartite quantum mutual information (as a function on the cone 𝔗+​(ℋA​B)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{AB})), which will be essentially used below.

Theorem 1. A) The limit relation

limk→∞I​(A:B)ωk=I​(A:B)ω0\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega^{k}}=I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega^{0}} (20)

holds for a sequence {ωk}⊂𝔗+​(ℋA​B)\{\omega^{k}\}\subset\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) converging to an operator ω0\omega^{0} if one of the following conditions is valid:

  1. a)

    limk→∞H⁡(ωXk)=H⁡(ωX0)<+∞\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(\omega_{X}^{k})=H(\omega_{X}^{0})<+\infty, where XX is one of the systems AA,BB (in this case the limit in (20) is finite according to (19));

  2. b)

    λk​ωk≤ΦAk⊗ΦBk​(ω0)\lambda_{k}\omega^{k}\leq\Phi_{A}^{k}\otimes\Phi_{B}^{k}(\omega^{0}) for some sequences {ΦAk}\{\Phi_{A}^{k}\} and {ΦBk}\{\Phi_{B}^{k}\} of local quantum operations and some sequence {λk}⊂[0,1]\{\lambda_{k}\}\subset[0,1]\hskip 1.0pt converging to 11.

B) If (20) holds for a sequence {ωk}⊂𝔗+​(ℋA​B)\{\omega^{k}\}\subset\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) as a finite limit then

limk→∞I​(A′:B′)ΦA⊗ΦB​(ωk)=I​(A′:B′)ΦA⊗ΦB​(ω0)<+∞\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}I(A^{\prime}\!:\!B^{\prime})_{\Phi_{A}\otimes\Phi_{B}(\omega^{k})}=I(A^{\prime}\!:\!B^{\prime})_{\Phi_{A}\otimes\Phi_{B}(\omega^{0})}<+\infty (21)

for arbitrary quantum operations ΦA:A→A′\,\Phi_{A}:A\rightarrow A^{\prime} and ΦB:B→B′\,\Phi_{B}:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}.

Theorem 4.1B states, briefly speaking, that local continuity of quantum mutual information is preserved by local operations.

Theorem 4.1 (proved in the Appendix) shows, in particular, that the quantum mutual information I​(A:B)ω\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} is continuous on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA​B)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) if and only if either AA or BB is a finite-dimensional system. Proposition 3 and upper bound (19) give the continuity bound for I​(A:B)ω\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} in this case.

Corollary 1. If one of the systems AA and BB, say AA, is finite-dimensional then I​(A:B)ω\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} is a continuous bounded function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA​B)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) and

|I​(A:B)ω1−I​(A:B)ω2|≤2​ε​log​dimℋA+3​(1+ε)​h2​(ε1+ε)|I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega^{1}}-I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega^{2}}|\leq 2\varepsilon\log\dim\mathcal{H}_{A}+3(1+\varepsilon)h_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right)

for any ω1,ω2∈𝔖⁡(ℋA​B)\,\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) such that ε=12​‖ω1−ω2‖1<1\;\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{1}-\omega^{2}\|_{1}<1\,, where h2​(⋅)\,h_{2}(\cdot)\, is the binary entropy.

Remark 3. The continuity conditions for I​(A:B)ω\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} in Theorem 4.1A coincides with the continuity condition for the Entanglement of Formation EF​(ω)\,E_{F}(\omega) of a state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite system [37, Sect.6].

The following example shows that condition a) in Theorem 4.1A is not necessary for existence of a finite limit in (20).

Example 1. Consider a sequence {ρk}⊂𝔖⁡(ℋA)\{\rho_{k}\}\subset\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) converging to a state ρ0\rho_{0} such that limk→∞H⁡(ρk)≠H⁡(ρ0)\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(\rho_{k})\neq H(\rho_{0}). By Lemma 2 there exists a sequence {ωk}⊂𝔖⁡(ℋA​B)\{\omega^{k}\}\subset\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}), ℋB≅ℋA\mathcal{H}_{B}\cong\mathcal{H}_{A}, converging to a state ω0∈𝔖⁡(ℋA​B)\omega^{0}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) such that ωAk=ρk\omega^{k}_{A}=\rho_{k} for all k≥0k\geq 0. Let σk=ωBk\sigma_{k}=\omega^{k}_{B} and ω~k=pk​ωk+(1−pk)​ρk⊗σk\,\tilde{\omega}^{k}=p_{k}\omega^{k}+(1-p_{k})\rho_{k}\otimes\sigma_{k}, where {pk}\{p_{k}\} is a sequence of positive numbers such that limk→∞pk​H​(ρk)=0\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}p_{k}H(\rho_{k})=0. The sequence {ω~k}\{\tilde{\omega}^{k}\} converges to the state ω~0=ρ0⊗σ0\tilde{\omega}^{0}=\rho_{0}\otimes\sigma_{0}. By using the convexity of the relative entropy it is easy to see that

limk→∞I​(A:B)ω~k=0=I​(A:B)ω~0\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\tilde{\omega}^{k}}=0=I(A\!:\!B)_{\tilde{\omega}^{0}}

while

limk→∞H⁡(ω~Ak)≠H⁡(ω~A0)andlimk→∞H⁡(ω~Bk)≠H⁡(ω~B0),\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(\tilde{\omega}_{A}^{k})\neq H(\tilde{\omega}_{A}^{0})\quad\textrm{and}\quad\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(\tilde{\omega}_{B}^{k})\neq H(\tilde{\omega}_{B}^{0}),

since ω~Ak=ρk\,\tilde{\omega}_{A}^{k}=\rho_{k}\, and ω~Bk=σk\,\tilde{\omega}_{B}^{k}=\sigma_{k}\, for all k≥0k\geq 0.

Condition b) in Theorem 4.1A implies the following observation used below.

Corollary 2. Let X\,X and YY be disjoint subsystems of A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n}. The function ωA1​…​An↦I​(X:Y)ω\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto I(X\!:\!Y)_{\omega} is faithful on 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}).66 6 See Def.3. In general faithfulness of the function ωX​Y↦F⁡(ωX​Y)\,\omega_{XY}\mapsto F(\omega_{XY}) does not imply faithfulness of the function ωA1​…​An↦F⁡(ωX​Y)\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto F(\omega_{XY}).

Proof. We may assume that X=A1X=A_{1} and Y=A2Y=A_{2}. The validity of relation (10) for the function ωA1​…​An↦I​(A1:A2)ω\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto I(A_{1}\!:\!A_{2})_{\omega} follows from the inequality

λk​ωA1​A2k≤PA1k⊗PA2k​ωA1​A2​PA1k⊗PA2k∀k,\lambda_{k}\omega^{k}_{A_{1}A_{2}}\leq P^{k}_{A_{1}}\otimes P^{k}_{A_{2}}\,\omega_{A_{1}A_{2}}\,P^{k}_{A_{1}}\otimes P^{k}_{A_{2}}\quad\forall k,

(where λk\lambda_{k} is defined in (10)) and condition b) in Theorem 4.1A.□\square

Remark 4. Corollary 4.1 and Lemma 2 show, by Lemma 3, that the function

ωA1​…​An↦∑kαk​I​(Xk:Yk)ω+∑kβk​H​(ωZk),\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}I(X_{k}\hskip 1.0pt:\hskip 1.0ptY_{k})_{\omega}+\sum_{k}\beta_{k}H(\omega_{Z_{k}}), (22)

where Xk,Yk,ZkX_{k},Y_{k},Z_{k} are subsystems of A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n}, is faithful on the set of all states at which it is well defined (the linear combination in (22) does not contain the uncertainty "​∞−∞​""\infty-\infty").

4.2 Multipartite case

Quantum mutual information of a state ωA1​…​An\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\, of a finite-dimensional nn-partite quantum system A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n} is defined as follows (cf. [7, 15, 33, 44])

I(A1:…:An)ω=∑i=1nH(ωAi)−H(ωA1​…​An).I(A_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:\ldots:\hskip 1.0ptA_{n})_{\omega}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(\omega_{A_{i}})-H(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}). (23)

In infinite dimensions it can be correctly defined for any state ωA1​…​An\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}} (as a value in [0,+∞][0,+\infty]) by the expression

I(A1:…:An)ω=H(ωA1​…​An∥ωA1⊗…⊗ωAn)I(A_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:\ldots:\hskip 1.0ptA_{n})_{\omega}=H(\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}}\otimes\ldots\otimes\omega_{A_{n}}\hskip 1.0pt) (24)

coinciding with (23) for any state ωA1​…​An\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}} with finite marginal entropies.

Quantity (23) can be extended to the cone 𝔗+​(ℋA1​…​An)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}}) by the formula

I(A1:…:An)ω=H(ωA1​…​An∥ωA1⊗…⊗ωAn[Tr​ωA1​…​An]n−1).I(A_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:\ldots:\hskip 1.0ptA_{n})_{\omega}=H\left(\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}}\,\|\;\frac{\omega_{A_{1}}\otimes\ldots\otimes\omega_{A_{n}}}{[\mathrm{Tr}\omega_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}}]^{n-1}}\hskip 1.0pt\right).

Basic properties of the relative entropy show that I(A1:…:An)ωI(A_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:\ldots:\hskip 1.0ptA_{n})_{\omega} is a lower semicontinuous function on the cone 𝔗+​(ℋA1​…​An)\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) taking values in [0,+∞][0,+\infty] and possessing the analogs of the above properties A1-A4. This can be shown by using the identity

I(A1:…:An)ω=I(A2:A1)ω+I(A3:A1A2)ω+…+I(An:A1…An−1)ωI(A_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:\ldots:\hskip 1.0ptA_{n})_{\omega}=I(A_{2}\hskip 1.0pt:\hskip 1.0ptA_{1})_{\omega}+I(A_{3}\hskip 1.0pt:\hskip 1.0ptA_{1}A_{2})_{\omega}+\ldots+I(A_{n}\hskip 1.0pt:\hskip 1.0ptA_{1}...A_{n-1})_{\omega}

which is directly verified for a state ω\omega with finite marginal entropies and can be extended to arbitrary states by approximation using Corollary 4.1. It follows from Lemma 3 that I(A1:…:An)ωI(A_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:\ldots:\hskip 1.0ptA_{n})_{\omega} defined by (24) is a 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of (23) to the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}}).

The above identity makes possible to obtain from (19) the upper bound

I(A1:…:An)ω≤2min1≤j≤n∑i≠jH(ωAi)I(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n})_{\omega}\leq 2\min_{1\leq j\leq n}\sum_{i\neq j}H(\omega_{A_{i}}) (25)

and to derive from Theorem 4.1 its nn-partite version.

Corollary 3. A) The limit relation

limk→∞I(A1:…:An)ωk=I(A1:…:An)ω0\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}I(A_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:...:\hskip 1.0ptA_{n})_{\omega^{k}}=I(A_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:...:\hskip 1.0ptA_{n})_{\omega^{0}} (26)

holds for a sequence {ωk}⊂𝔗+​(ℋA1​…​An)\{\omega^{k}\}\subset\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) converging to an operator ω0\,\omega^{0} if one of the following conditions is valid:

  1. a)

    limk→∞H⁡(ωAik)=H⁡(ωAi0)<+∞\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(\omega_{A_{i}}^{k})=H(\omega_{A_{i}}^{0})<+\infty\, for at least n−1\,n\!-\!1\, values of i\;i (in this case the limit in (26) is finite according to (25)); 77 7 It is easy to see that validity of this relation for n−2\,n\!-\!2\, values of i\,i does not imply (26).

  2. b)

    λk​ωk≤ΦA1k⊗…⊗ΦAnk​(ω0)\lambda_{k}\omega^{k}\leq\Phi_{A_{1}}^{k}\otimes...\otimes\Phi_{A_{n}}^{k}(\omega^{0}) for some sequences {ΦA1k}\{\Phi_{A_{1}}^{k}\},…,{ΦAnk}\{\Phi_{A_{n}}^{k}\} of local quantum operations and some sequence {λk}⊂[0,1]\{\lambda_{k}\}\subset[0,1]\hskip 1.0pt converging to 11.

B) If (26) holds for a sequence {ωk}⊂𝔗+​(ℋA1​…​An)\{\omega^{k}\}\subset\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) as a finite limit then

limk→∞I(A1′:…:An′)ΦA1⊗…⊗ΦAn​(ωk)=I(A1′:…:An′)ΦA1⊗…⊗ΦAn​(ω0)\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}I(A^{\prime}_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:...:\hskip 1.0ptA^{\prime}_{n})_{\Phi_{A_{1}}\otimes...\otimes\Phi_{A_{n}}(\omega^{k})}=I(A^{\prime}_{1}\hskip 1.0pt:...:\hskip 1.0ptA^{\prime}_{n})_{\Phi_{A_{1}}\otimes...\otimes\Phi_{A_{n}}(\omega^{0})}

for arbitrary quantum operations ΦA1:A1→A1′,…,ΦAn:An→An′\Phi_{A_{1}}:A_{1}\rightarrow A^{\prime}_{1},...,\Phi_{A_{n}}:A_{n}\rightarrow A^{\prime}_{n}.

Corollary 4.2B states that local operations do not destroy continuity of the multipartite quantum mutual information (similar to the bipartite case).

By using the condition b) in Corollary 4.2A one can generalize Corollary 4.1, i.e. to show global faithfulness of the function ωA1​…​An↦I(Ai1:…:Aim)ω\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto I(A_{i_{1}}\hskip 1.0pt:...:\hskip 1.0ptA_{i_{m}})_{\omega} for any subsystems Ai1,…,Aim\,A_{i_{1}},...,A_{i_{m}} of A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n}.

Proposition 3 and upper bound (25) imply the following result.

Corollary 4. If n−1\,n-1\, subsystems, say A1,…,An−1A_{1},...,A_{n-1}, are finite-dimensional then I(A1:…:An)ωI(A_{1}\!:\!...\!:\!A_{n})_{\omega} is a continuous bounded function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) and

|I(A1:…:An)ω1−I(A1:…:An)ω2|≤2εC+(n+1)(1+ε)h2(ε1+ε)|I(A_{1}\!:\!...\!:\!A_{n})_{\omega^{1}}-I(A_{1}\!:\!...\!:\!A_{n})_{\omega^{2}}|\leq 2\varepsilon C+(n+1)(1+\varepsilon)h_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right)

for any ω1,ω2∈𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\,\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) such that ε=12​‖ω1−ω2‖1<1\;\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{1}-\omega^{2}\|_{1}<1\,, where h2​(⋅)\,h_{2}(\cdot)\, is the binary entropy and C=logdimℋA1​…​An−1\,C=\log\dim\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n-1}}.

4.3 General relations between conditional and unconditional quantities

For a quantity F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαk​H​(ωXk)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}) introduce the corresponding conditional quantity

F⋅|B​(ωA1​…​An​B)=∑kαk​[H⁡(ωXk​B)−H⁡(ωB)].F_{\cdot|B}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}\!\left[H(\omega_{X_{k}B})-H(\omega_{B})\right]. (27)

By considering FF as a function of ωA1​…​An​B\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\, we have

[F⋅|B−F](ωA1​…​An​B)=−∑kαk[H(ωXk)+H(ωB)−H(ωXk​B)]\left[F_{\cdot|B}-F\right]\!(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B})=-\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}\!\left[H(\omega_{X_{k}})+H(\omega_{B})-H(\omega_{X_{k}B})\right]

for any state with finite marginal entropies. Hence, Remark 4.1, upper bound (19) and Theorem 4.1 imply the following observation.

Proposition 2. The difference [F⋅|B−F]\left[F_{\cdot|B}-F\right] has the finite 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension

[F⋅|B−F](ωA1​…​An​B)=−∑kαkI(Xk:B)ω\left[F_{\cdot|B}-F\right]\!(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B})=-\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}I(X_{k}\!:\!B)_{\omega} (28)

to the set {ωA1​…​An​B|min⁡{H⁡(ωB),∑kH⁡(ωXk)}<+∞}\,\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\,|\,\min\left\{H(\omega_{B}),\sum_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}})\right\}<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\right\} possessing the properties:

  1. 1)

    |[F⋅|B−F]​(ωA1​…​An​B)|≤min⁡{H⁡(ωB)​[|∑kαk|+∑k|αk|],2​∑k|αk|​H​(ωXk)}\left|\!\left[F_{\cdot|B}-F\right]\!(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B})\right|\leq\min\{H(\omega_{B})\!\left[|\sum_{k}\!\alpha_{k}|+\!\sum_{k}\!|\alpha_{k}|\right]\!,2\sum_{k}\!|\alpha_{k}|H(\omega_{X_{k}})\};

  2. 2)

    the function ωA1​…​An​B↦[F⋅|B−F]​(ωA1​…​An​B)\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\mapsto\left[F_{\cdot|B}-F\right]\!(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}) is continuous on a subset 𝒜⊂𝔗+​(ℋA1​…​An​B)\mathcal{A}\subset\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}) if one the following conditions holds:

    1. a)

      the function ωA1​…​An​B↦H⁡(ωB)\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\mapsto H(\omega_{B}) is continuous on 𝒜\mathcal{A};

    2. b)

      the functions ωA1​…​An​B↦H⁡(ωXk)\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\mapsto H(\omega_{X_{k}}) is continuous on 𝒜\mathcal{A} for all k\,k.

Proposition 4.3 with condition a) shows, roughly speaking, that conditioning upon a system with finite (corresp. continuous) entropy does not destroy finiteness (corresp. continuity) of a quantity F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαk​H​(ωXk)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}).

Proposition 4.3 with condition b) shows that finiteness (corresp. continuity) of all marginal entropies in a linear combination F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαk​H​(ωXk)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}) guarantees finiteness (corresp. continuity) of the conditional quantity F⋅|BF_{\cdot|B} regardless of the system BB.

By Proposition 4.3 the formula

F⋅|B​(ωA1​…​An​B)=∑kαk​[H⁡(ωXk)−I​(Xk:B)ω]F_{\cdot|B}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}\left[H(\omega_{X_{k}})-I(X_{k}\!:\!B)_{\omega}\right] (29)

defines the 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of (27) to the set {ωA1​…​An​B|maxk⁡H⁡(ωXk)<+∞}\,\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\,|\,\max_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}})<+\infty\right\}.

Note: Proposition 4.3 does not assert the existence of 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of quantity (27) to the set {ωA1​…​An​B|H⁡(ωB)<+∞}\,\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\,|\,H(\omega_{B})<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\}.

5 Extended quantum conditional entropy

The quantum conditional entropy

H​(A|B)ω=H⁡(ωA​B)−H⁡(ωB)H(A|B)_{\omega}=H(\omega_{AB})-H(\omega_{B}) (30)

of a state of a finite-dimensional bipartite system A​BAB is essentially used in analysis of quantum systems and channels despite its possible negativity [16, 33]. It has the following basic properties:

  1. B1)

    concavity: H​(A|B)p​ω1+(1−p)​ω2≥p​H​(A|B)ω1+(1−p)​H​(A|B)ω2H(A|B)_{p\omega_{1}+(1-p)\omega_{2}}\geq pH(A|B)_{\omega_{1}}+(1-p)H(A|B)_{\omega_{2}};

  2. B2)

    monotonicity: H​(A|B)ω≥H​(A|B​C)ω,ω=ωA​B​CH(A|B)_{\omega}\geq H(A|BC)_{\omega},\;\,\omega=\omega_{ABC};

  3. B3)

    subadditivity: H​(A​A′|B​B′)ω≤H​(A|B)ω+H​(A′|B′)ω,ω=ωA​A′​B​B′H(AA^{\prime}|BB^{\prime})_{\omega}\leq H(A|B)_{\omega}+H(A^{\prime}|B^{\prime})_{\omega},\;\,\omega=\omega_{AA^{\prime}BB^{\prime}}.

In infinite dimensions formula (30) defines a finite quantity possessing properties B1-B3 on the set 𝔖f={ωA​B|max⁡{H⁡(ωA),H⁡(ωB)}<+∞}\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}}=\{\omega_{AB}\,|\,\max\{H(\omega_{A}),H(\omega_{B})\}<+\infty\}. This narrow domain of definition of H​(A|B)ωH(A|B)_{\omega} is extended in [27], where it is shown that the quantity

He(A|B)ω=H(ωA)−H(ωA​B∥ωA⊗ωB)=H(ωA)−I(A:B)ωH_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B)_{\omega}=H(\omega_{A})-H(\omega_{AB}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B})=H(\omega_{A})-I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} (31)

coinciding with (30) on 𝔖f\mathfrak{S}_{\mathrm{f}} possesses properties B1-B3 on the convex set {ωA​B|H⁡(ωA)<+∞}\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{AB}\,|\,H(\omega_{A})<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\} containing states with H⁡(ωA​B)=H⁡(ωB)=+∞H(\omega_{AB})=H(\omega_{B})=+\infty. This extension turns out to be very useful in the analysis of infinite-dimensional quantum systems and channels [12, 21].88 8 This extension of the quantum conditional entropy plays a basic role of the proof of the generalized version of the Bennett-Shor-Smolin-Thaplyal theorem given in [21]. Note that (31) is a partial case of (29) for F⁡(ωA)=H⁡(ωA)F(\omega_{A})=H(\omega_{A}).

Proposition 1 in [27] and Proposition 4.3 imply the following observations.

Proposition 3. A) The quantity He​(A|B)ωH_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B)_{\omega} defined by (31) is a 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of the quantum conditional entropy (30) to the set {ωA​B|H⁡(ωA)<+∞}\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{AB}\,|\,H(\omega_{A})<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\} possessing properties B1-B3 such that |He​(A|B)ω|≤H⁡(ωA)|H_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B)_{\omega}|\leq H(\omega_{A}).

B) Local continuity of H⁡(ωA)H(\omega_{A}) implies local continuity of He​(A|B)ωH_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B)_{\omega}.

Continuity bound for the conditional entropy defined by formula (30) under the condition dimℋA<+∞\,\dim\mathcal{H}_{A}<+\infty\, was originally obtained by Alicki and Fannes in [3] and then was strengthened by Winter in [43]. Proposition 3 gives the continuity bound for the extended quantum conditional entropy coinciding with Winter’s continuity bound.99 9 So, Corollary 5 generalizes Winter’s continuity bound to the case H⁡(ωB)=+∞\,H(\omega_{B})=+\infty\,. It can be directly derived from Lemma 2 in [43] by approximation.

Corollary 5. If the system AA is finite-dimensional then He​(A|B)ω\,H_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B)_{\omega} is a continuous bounded function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA​B)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) and

|He​(A|B)ω1−He​(A|B)ω2|≤2​ε​log​dimℋA+(1+ε)​h2​(ε1+ε)|H_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B)_{\omega^{1}}-H_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B)_{\omega^{2}}|\leq 2\varepsilon\log\dim\mathcal{H}_{A}+(1+\varepsilon)\hskip 1.0pth_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right) (32)

for any ω1,ω2∈𝔖⁡(ℋA​B)\,\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{AB}) such that ε=12​‖ω1−ω2‖1<1\;\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{1}-\omega^{2}\|_{1}<1\,, where h2​(⋅)\,h_{2}(\cdot)\, is the binary entropy.

Besides the above-mentioned direct applications the function He​(A|B)ωH_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B)_{\omega} can be used for construction of 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extensions for linear combinations of marginal entropies of a special form. By Remark 4.1 the function

ωA1​…​An↦∑kαk​He​(Xk|Yk)ω,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H_{\mathrm{e}}(X_{k}|Y_{k})_{\omega}, (33)

where Xk,YkX_{k},Y_{k} are disjoint subsystems of A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n}, is faithful on the set of all states for which H⁡(ωXk)<+∞\,H(\omega_{X_{k}})<+\infty for all kk. This and Proposition 5 imply the following observation.

Proposition 4. If a quantity F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαk​H​(ωXk)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}) can be represented as follows

F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=β1​H​(ωAi0)+∑k>1βk​[H⁡(ωAi0​Yk)−H⁡(ωYk)],F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\beta_{1}H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}})+\sum_{k>1}\beta_{k}\!\left[H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}Y_{k}})-H(\omega_{Y_{k}})\right], (34)

where YkY_{k} is a particular subsystem of A1​…​An\Ai0A_{1}...A_{n}\backslash A_{i_{0}} for all k\,k, then FF has the 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension

F^​(ωA1​…​An)=β1​H​(ωAi0)+∑k>1βk​He​(Ai0|Yk)ω\widehat{F}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\beta_{1}H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}})+\sum_{k>1}\beta_{k}H_{\mathrm{e}}(A_{i_{0}}|Y_{k})_{\omega}

to the set {ωA1​…​An|H⁡(ωAi0)<+∞}\,\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\,|\,H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}})<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\} possessing the properties:

  1. 1)

    |F^​(ωA1​…​An)|≤H⁡(ωAi0)​∑k≥1|βk||\widehat{F}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})|\leq H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}})\sum_{k\geq 1}|\beta_{k}|;

  2. 2)

    local continuity of the function ωA1​…​An↦H⁡(ωAi0)\;\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}}) implies local continuity of the function ωA1​…​An↦F^​(ωA1​…​An)\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto\widehat{F}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}).

Remark 5. If a quantity F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαk​H​(ωXk)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}) has representation (34) for some index i0i_{0} then the corresponding conditional quantity (27) also has representation (34) for the same index i0i_{0} and hence, by Proposition 5, it has the 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension to the set {ωA1​…​An​B|H⁡(ωAi0)<+∞}\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\,|\,H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}})<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\} possessing the above properties 1) and 2) (with ωA1​…​An​B\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B} instead of ωA1​…​An\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}). □\square

For a quantity F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαk​H​(ωXk)F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}}) consider the ”reduced” quantity

F⋅\Ai0(ωA1​…​An)=∑kαkH(ωXk\Ai0),F_{\cdot\backslash A_{i_{0}}}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}H(\omega_{X_{k}\backslash A_{i_{0}}}),

where ωXk\Ai0=TrAi0​ωXk\,\omega_{X_{k}\backslash A_{i_{0}}}=\mathrm{Tr}_{A_{i_{0}}}\omega_{X_{k}} if Ai0⊆XkA_{i_{0}}\subseteq X_{k} and ωXk\Ai0=ωXk\,\omega_{X_{k}\backslash A_{i_{0}}}=\omega_{X_{k}} otherwise. We have

[F⋅\Ai0−F](ωA1​…​An)=∑k∈K⁡(i0)αk[H(ωXk\Ai0)−H(ωXk)],\left[F_{\cdot\backslash A_{i_{0}}}-F\right]\!(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{k\in K(i_{0})}\alpha_{k}\!\left[H(\omega_{X_{k}\backslash A_{i_{0}}})-H(\omega_{X_{k}})\right]\!,

where K⁡(i0)≐{k|Ai0⊆Xk}K(i_{0})\doteq\{\hskip 1.0ptk\hskip 1.0pt|\hskip 1.0ptA_{i_{0}}\subseteq X_{k}\hskip 1.0pt\}, i.e. the difference [F⋅\Ai0−F]\left[F_{\cdot\backslash A_{i_{0}}}-F\right] has representation (34). So, Proposition 5 implies the following observation used below.

Corollary 6. The difference [F⋅\Ai0−F]\left[F_{\cdot\backslash A_{i_{0}}}-F\right] has the finite 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension

[F⋅\Ai0−F](ωA1​…​An)=−∑k∈K⁡(i0)αkHe(Ai0|Xk\Ai0)ω\left[F_{\cdot\backslash A_{i_{0}}}-F\right]\!(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=-\sum_{k\in K(i_{0})}\alpha_{k}H_{\mathrm{e}}(A_{i_{0}}|X_{k}\backslash A_{i_{0}})_{\omega}

to the set {ωA1​…​An|H⁡(ωAi0)<+∞}\,\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\,|\,H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}})<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\} possessing the properties:

  1. 1)

    |[F⋅\Ai0−F](ωA1​…​An)|≤H(ωAi0)∑k∈K⁡(i0)|αk|\left|\left[F_{\cdot\backslash A_{i_{0}}}-F\right]\!(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})\right|\leq H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}})\sum_{k\in K(i_{0})}|\alpha_{k}|;

  2. 2)

    local continuity of the function ωA1​…​An↦H⁡(ωAi0)\;\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}}) implies local continuity of the function ωA1​…​An↦[F⋅\Ai0−F](ωA1​…​An)\;\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto\left[F_{\cdot\backslash A_{i_{0}}}-F\right]\!(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}).

Corollary 5 shows, roughly speaking, that reducing a system with finite (corresp. continuous) entropy does not destroy finiteness (corresp. continuity) of any quantity FF defined as a linear combination of marginal entropies.

Note: Corollary 5 does not assert the existence of 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extensions to the set {ωA1​…​An|H⁡(ωAi0)<+∞}\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\,|\,H(\omega_{A_{i_{0}}})<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\} for the quantities FF and F⋅\Ai0F_{\cdot\backslash A_{i_{0}}} separately.

6 Conditional mutual information

6.1 Tripartite system

The conditional mutual information of a state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} of a tripartite finite-dimensional system A​B​CABC is defined as follows

I(A:C|B)ω≐H(ωA​B)+H(ωB​C)−H(ωA​B​C)−H(ωB).I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\doteq H(\omega_{AB})+H(\omega_{BC})-H(\omega_{ABC})-H(\omega_{B}). (35)

This quantity plays important role in different branches of quantum information theory [9, 10, 11, 15, 39, 44, 46], it has the following basic properties:

  1. C1)

    I(A:C|B)ω≥0I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\geq 0 for any state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} and I(A:C|B)ω=0I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=0 if and only if there is a channel Φ:B→B​C\Phi:B\rightarrow BC such that ωA​B​C=IdA⊗Φ⁡(ωA​B)\omega_{ABC}=\mathrm{Id}_{A}\otimes\Phi(\omega_{AB}) [13];

  2. C2)

    monotonicity under local conditioning: I(AB:C)ω≥I(A:C|B)ωI(AB\!:\!C)_{\omega}\geq I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega};

  3. C3)

    monotonicity under local operations: I(A:C|B)ω≥I(A′:C′|B)ΦA⊗IdB⊗ΦC​(ω)I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\geq I(A^{\prime}\!:\!C^{\prime}|B)_{\Phi_{A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{\!B}\otimes\Phi_{C}(\omega)} for arbitrary quantum operations ΦA:A→A′\Phi_{A}:A\rightarrow A^{\prime} and ΦC:C→C′\Phi_{C}:C\rightarrow C^{\prime};1010 10 If either ΦA\Phi_{A} or ΦC\Phi_{C} is a trace non-preserving operation then I(A′:C′|B)ΦA⊗IdB⊗ΦC​(ω)I(A^{\prime}\!:\!C^{\prime}|B)_{\Phi_{A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{\!B}\otimes\Phi_{C}(\omega)} is defined by (35), where HH is the extended von Neumann entropy (5), see Remark 2.

  4. C4)

    additivity: I(AA′:CC′|BB′)ω⊗ω′=I(A:C|B)ω+I(A′:C′|B′)ω′I(AA^{\prime}\!:\!CC^{\prime}|BB^{\prime})_{\omega\otimes\omega^{\prime}}=I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}+I(A^{\prime}\!:\!C^{\prime}|B^{\prime})_{\omega^{\prime}};

  5. C5)

    duality: I(A:C|B)ω=I(A:C|D)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=I(A\!:\!C|D)_{\omega} for any pure state ωA​B​C​D\omega_{ABCD} [10].

The nonnegativity of I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} is a basic result of quantum information theory well known as strong subadditivity of von Neumann entropy [30].

The conditional mutual information (35) can be represented by one of the formulae

I(A:C|B)ω=I(A:BC)ω−I(A:B)ω,I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=I(A\!:\!BC)_{\omega}-I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}, (36)
I(A:C|B)ω=I(AB:C)ω−I(B:C)ω.I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=I(AB\!:\!C)_{\omega}-I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega}. (37)

By these representations, the nonnegativity of I(A:C|B)I(A\!:\!C|B) is a direct corollary of the monotonicity of the relative entropy under partial trace.1111 11 The monotonicity of the quantum relative entropy and the strong subadditivity of the von Neumann entropy are globally equivalent [16].

Formula (28) in this case implies

I(A:C|B)ω=I(A:C)ω−I(A:B)ω−I(C:B)ω+I(AC:B)ω.I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=I(A\!:\!C)_{\omega}-I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}-I(C\!:\!B)_{\omega}+I(AC\!:\!B)_{\omega}. (38)

The quantity I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} defined in (35) can be also represented as follows

I(A:C|B)ω=I(A:C)ω+I(AB:D)ω~+I(BC:D)ω~+I​(A​C:D)ω~−4​H​(ωA​B​C),\begin{array}[]{c}I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=I(A\!:\!C)_{\omega}+I(AB\!:\!D)_{\tilde{\omega}}+I(BC\!:\!D)_{\tilde{\omega}}\\ \\ +I(AC\!:\!D)_{\tilde{\omega}}-4H(\omega_{ABC}),\end{array} (39)

where ω~=ω~A​B​C​D\tilde{\omega}=\tilde{\omega}_{ABCD} is any purification of the state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC}.

In infinite dimensions the quantity I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} is well defined by formula (35) as a faithful function (Def.3) on the set

𝔖0={ωA​B​C|H(ωA​B​C)<+∞,H(ωB)<+∞}.\mathfrak{S}_{0}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,H(\omega_{ABC})<+\infty,H(\omega_{B})<+\infty\right\}.

By Remark 4.1 formulae (36), (37), (38), (39) define 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extensions of (35) respectively to the sets

𝔖1={ωA​B​C|I​(A:B)ω<+∞},𝔖2={ωA​B​C|I​(B:C)ω<+∞},𝔖3={ωA​B​C|H⁡(ωB)<+∞},𝔖4={ωA​B​C|H⁡(ωA​B​C)<+∞}.\begin{array}[]{ll}\mathfrak{S}_{1}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}<+\infty\right\},&\quad\mathfrak{S}_{2}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega}<+\infty\right\},\\ \\ \mathfrak{S}_{3}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,H(\omega_{B})<+\infty\right\},&\quad\mathfrak{S}_{4}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,H(\omega_{ABC})<+\infty\right\}.\end{array}

The following theorem shows that formulae (35)-(39) agree with each other (coincide on the sets 𝔖i∩𝔖j\mathfrak{S}_{i}\cap\mathfrak{S}_{j}) and can be extended to a unique lower semicontinuous function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA​B​C)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC}) possessing basis properties of the conditional mutual information.

Theorem 2. There exists a unique lower semicontinuous functionIe(A:C|B)ωI_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA​B​C)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC}) such that:

    Ie(A:C|B)ωI_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} coincides with I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} given by (35),(36), (37), (38), (39) respectively on the sets 𝔖0,𝔖1,𝔖2,𝔖3,𝔖4\,\mathfrak{S}_{0},\mathfrak{S}_{1},\mathfrak{S}_{2},\mathfrak{S}_{3},\mathfrak{S}_{4};

  • •

    Ie(A:C|B)ωI_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} possesses the above-stated properties C1-C5 of conditional mutual information.

Ie(A:C|B)ω=supPA[I(A:BC)Q​ω​Q−I(A:B)Q​ω​Q],Q=PA⊗IB⊗IC,I_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=\sup_{P_{A}}\left[\hskip 1.0ptI(A\!:\!BC)_{Q\omega Q}-I(A\!:\!B)_{Q\omega Q}\hskip 1.0pt\right]\!,\;\,Q=P_{A}\otimes I_{B}\otimes I_{C}, (40)

Corollary 10. A) The function ω↦[I​(A:B​C)ω−I​(A:B)ω]\,\omega\mapsto\left[\hskip 1.0ptI(A\!:\!BC)_{\omega}-I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}\right] is lower semicontinuous on the set {ω∈𝔗+​(ℋA​B​C)|I​(A:B)ω<+∞}\,\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega\in\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC})\,|\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}<+\infty\hskip 1.0pt\}.

Proof. Assertion A follows from Theorem 6.1 and formula (36). By Lemma 2 assertion B follows from A and the lower semicontinuity of quantum mutual information. Assertion C follows from B and Theorem 4.1A. □\square.

6.2 Multipartite system

The conditional mutual information of a state ωA1​…​An​B\,\omega_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}B}\, of a finite-dimensional multipartite system A1​…​An​BA_{1}\ldots A_{n}B is defined as follows

I(A1:…:An|B)ω≐∑i=1nH​(Ai|B)ω−H​(A1​…​An|B)ω=∑i=1nH⁡(ωAi​B)−H⁡(ωA1​…​An​B)−(n−1)​H​(ωB).\begin{array}[]{cl}I(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega}&\doteq\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(A_{i}|B)_{\omega}-H(A_{1}\ldots A_{n}|B)_{\omega}\\ &=\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(\omega_{A_{i}B})-H(\omega_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}B})-(n-1)H(\omega_{B}).\end{array} (48)

The analogs of the above-mentioned properties C1-C4 of the tripartite conditional mutual information can be proved for I(A1:…:An|B)ωI(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega} by using the representation (cf. [44])

I(A1:…:An|B)ω=I(A2:A1|B)ω+I(A3:A1A2|B)ω+…+I(An:A1…An−1|B)ω.\begin{array}[]{rl}I(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega}=I(A_{2}\!:\!A_{1}|B)_{\omega}&+\;I(A_{3}\!:\!A_{1}A_{2}|B)_{\omega}+...\\ \\ &+\;I(A_{n}\!:\!A_{1}...A_{n-1}|B)_{\omega}.\end{array} (49)

and its modifications obtained by permuting indexes in the right hand side.

Formula (28) in this case has the form

I(A1:…:An|B)ω−I(A1:…:An)ω=I(A1…An:B)ω−∑i=1nI(Ai:B)ω.I(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega}-I(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n})_{\omega}=I(A_{1}...A_{n}\!:\!B)_{\omega}-\sum_{i=1}^{n}I(A_{i}\!:\!B)_{\omega}. (50)

Since (49) is valid with arbitrarily permuted indexes  1,…,n\,1,...,n\, in the right hand side, Remark 6.1 implies that I(A1:…:An|B)ωI(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega} is upper bounded by the value

2​min⁡∑i≠j1≤j≤n⁡min⁡{H⁡(ωAi),H⁡(ωAi​B)}.2\min_{1\leq j\leq n}\sum_{i\neq j}\min\left\{H(\omega_{A_{i}}),H(\omega_{A_{i}B})\right\}. (51)

By using representation (49) and the extended conditional mutual information described in Theorem 6.1 one can define I(A1:…:An|B)ω\,I(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega} for any state of an infinite-dimensional system A1​…​An​BA_{1}...A_{n}B.

Proposition 5. 7 Other information measures in multipartite systems

7.1 Quantum version of interaction information

Consider the following characteristic of a state ωA1​…​An\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}} of nn-partite quantum system

In​(ωA1​…​An)=∑iH⁡(ωAi)−∑i<jH⁡(ωAi​Aj)+∑i<j<kH(ωAi​Aj​Ak)−…−(−1)nH(ωA1​…​An)\begin{array}[]{rl}I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})&\displaystyle=\sum_{i}H(\omega_{A_{i}})-\sum_{i<j}H(\omega_{A_{i}A_{j}})\\ &\displaystyle+\sum_{i<j<k}H(\omega_{A_{i}A_{j}A_{k}})-...-(-1)^{n}H(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})\end{array} (53)

which (up to the sign) can be considered as a noncommutative version of the interaction information of a nn-partite classical system [22, 32].

Note that I1​(ωA)I_{1}(\omega_{A}) is the von Neumann entropy of a one-partite state ωA\omega_{A}, I2​(ωA​B)I_{2}(\omega_{AB}) is the quantum mutual information of a bipartite state ωA​B\omega_{AB}, while

I3​(ωA​B​C)=H⁡(ωA)+H⁡(ωB)+H⁡(ωC)−H⁡(ωA​B)−H⁡(ωA​C)−H⁡(ωB​C)+H⁡(ωA​B​C)\begin{array}[]{rl}I_{3}(\omega_{ABC})&=H(\omega_{A})+H(\omega_{B})+H(\omega_{C})\\ \\ &-\,H(\omega_{AB})-H(\omega_{AC})-H(\omega_{BC})+H(\omega_{ABC})\end{array}

is the topological entanglement entropy of a tripartite state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} typically denoted Htopo​(ωA​B​C)H_{\mathrm{topo}}(\omega_{ABC}) (or Stopo​(ωA​B​C)S_{\mathrm{topo}}(\omega_{ABC})) [23]. Despite possible negativity the last quantity is also used as a special measure of quantum correlations [6, 14].

An interesting feature of the linear combinations of marginal entropies in (53) consists in the fact that for any nn finiteness of only one marginal entropy H⁡(ωAi)H(\omega_{A_{i}}) ”eliminates” all possible uncertainties "​∞−∞​""\infty-\infty" in (53), while continuity of H⁡(ωAi)H(\omega_{A_{i}}) guarantees continuity of In​(ωA1​…​An)I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}).

Proposition 6. A) The quantity In​(ωA1​…​An)I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) defined in (53) has finite 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension to the set {ωA1​…​An|∃i:H(ωAi)<+∞}\,\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\,|\,\exists\hskip 1.0pti:H(\omega_{A_{i}})<+\infty\}\, such that 1515 15 We denote this 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of In​(ωA1​…​An)I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) by the same symbol.

|In​(ωA1​…​An)|≤2n−1​min⁡{H⁡(ωA1),…,H⁡(ωAn)}.|I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})|\leq 2^{n-1}\min\{H(\omega_{A_{1}}),\ldots,H(\omega_{A_{n}})\}.

In​(ωA1​…​An)=H⁡(ωAi)−∑jHe​(Ai|Aj)ω+∑j<kHe​(Ai|Ak​Aj)ω−∑j<k<lHe(Ai|AjAkAl)ω+…+(−1)n−1He(Ai|A1…Ai−1Ai+1…An)ω,\begin{array}[]{c}I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})\displaystyle=H(\omega_{A_{i}})-\sum_{j}H_{\mathrm{e}}(A_{i}|A_{j})_{\omega}+\sum_{j<k}H_{\mathrm{e}}(A_{i}|A_{k}A_{j})_{\omega}\\ \displaystyle-\sum_{j<k<l}H_{\mathrm{e}}(A_{i}|A_{j}A_{k}A_{l})_{\omega}+...+(-1)^{n-1}H_{\mathrm{e}}(A_{i}|A_{1}...A_{i-1}A_{i+1}...A_{n})_{\omega},\end{array} (54)

where all the indexes k,j,l,…k,j,l,... in each sum run over the set {1,…,n}∖{i}\{1,...,n\}\setminus\{i\} and He​(X|Y)ωH_{\mathrm{e}}(X|Y)_{\omega} is the extended quantum conditional entropy defined by (31).

C) Local continuity of one of the marginal entropies H⁡(ωA1),…,H⁡(ωAn)\,H(\omega_{A_{1}}),...,H(\omega_{A_{n}}) implies local continuity of In​(ωA1​…​An)\,I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}).

Proof. A) Assume that H⁡(ωAn)H(\omega_{A_{n}}) is finite. Consider the quantity

F⁡(ωA1​…​An)=H⁡(ωAn)+In−1​(ωA1​…​An−1)−In​(ωA1​…​An)=∑i<nH⁡(ωAi​An)−∑i<j<nH(ωAi​Aj​An)+∑i<j<k<nH(ωAi​Aj​Ak​An)−…−(−1)n−1H(ωA1​…​An).\begin{array}[]{c}\displaystyle F(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=H(\omega_{A_{n}})+I_{n-1}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n-1}})-I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=\sum_{i<n}H(\omega_{A_{i}A_{n}})\\ \\ \displaystyle-\sum_{i<j<n}H(\omega_{A_{i}A_{j}A_{n}})+\sum_{i<j<k<n}H(\omega_{A_{i}A_{j}A_{k}A_{n}})-...-(-1)^{n-1}H(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}).\end{array}

In terms of Corollary 5 we have F⋅\An=In−1F_{\cdot\backslash A_{n}}=I_{n-1} and hence

In(ωA1​…​An)=H(ωAn)+[F⋅\An−F](ωA1​…​An).I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})=H(\omega_{A_{n}})+[F_{\cdot\backslash A_{n}}-F\hskip 1.0pt](\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}). (55)

So, Corollary 5 implies the existence of 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of the quantity In​(ωA1​…​An)I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) defined in (53) to the set {ωA1​…​An|H⁡(ωAn)<+∞}\,\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\,|\,H(\omega_{A_{n}})<+\infty\}\, determined by formula (54) with i=n\,i=n\, such that

|In​(ωA1​…​An)|≤2n−1​H​(ωAn).|I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}})|\leq 2^{n-1}H(\omega_{A_{n}}).

To complete the proof of A it suffices to note that the 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extensions of InI_{n} to the sets {ωA1​…​An|H⁡(ωAi)<+∞}\,\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\,|\,H(\omega_{A_{i}})<+\infty\}\, and {ωA1​…​An|H⁡(ωAj)<+∞}\,\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\,|\,H(\omega_{A_{j}})<+\infty\}\, agree with each other by Lemma 3.

B) If the function ωA1​…​An↦H⁡(ωAn)\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto H(\omega_{A_{n}}) is continuous on a set 𝒜\mathcal{A} then Corollary 5 and (55) imply continuity of the function ωA1​…​An↦In​(ωA1​…​An)\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}\mapsto I_{n}(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) on 𝒜\mathcal{A}. □\square

for any ω1,ω2∈𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An)\,\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}) such that ε=12​‖ω1−ω2‖1<1\;\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{1}-\omega^{2}\|_{1}<1\,, where h2​(⋅)\,h_{2}(\cdot)\, is the binary entropy.

7.2 Secrecy monotone SnS_{n} (unconditional and conditional)

Along with the quantum mutual information I(A1:…:An)I(A_{1}\!:\!\ldots\!:\!A_{n}) the secrecy monotone

Sn(A1:…:An)ω=∑i=1nH(ωA1​…​Ai−1​Ai+1​…​An)−(n−1)H(ωA1​…​An)S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n})_{\omega}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{i-1}A_{i+1}...A_{n}})-(n-1)H(\omega_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}})

is proposed in [7] as a measure of quantum correlations of a state ωA1​…​An\omega_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}} of a finite-dimensional nn-partite system.1616 16 The same quantity is independently proposed and analyzed in [26], where it is called ”operational quantum mutual information”. Note that S2​(A1:A2)ω=I​(A1:A2)ωS_{2}(A_{1}\!:\!A_{2})_{\omega}=I(A_{1}\!:\!A_{2})_{\omega}, so, the quantity SnS_{n} can be considered as a particular nn-partite generalization of the bipartite quantum mutual information. It can be expressed as follows

Sn(A1:…:An)ω=I(A1:A2…An)ω+I(A2:A3…An|A1)ω+I(A3:A4…An|A1A2)ω+…+I(An−1:An|A1…An−2)ω.\begin{array}[]{c}S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n})_{\omega}=I(A_{1}\!:\!A_{2}...A_{n})_{\omega}+\;I(A_{2}\!:\!A_{3}...A_{n}|A_{1})_{\omega}\\ \\ +I(A_{3}\!:\!A_{4}...A_{n}|A_{1}A_{2})_{\omega}+...+I(A_{n-1}\!:\!A_{n}|A_{1}...A_{n-2})_{\omega}.\end{array} (56)

In applications the conditional version of SnS_{n}, i.e. the characteristic

Sn(A1:…:An|B)ω=∑i=1nH⁡(ωA1​…​Ai−1​Ai+1​…​An​B)−(n−1)​H​(ωA1​…​An​B)−H⁡(ωB).\begin{array}[]{rl}S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega}&\displaystyle=\,\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(\omega_{A_{1}...A_{i-1}A_{i+1}...A_{n}B})\\ \\ &\displaystyle-\;(n-1)H(\omega_{A_{1}\ldots A_{n}B})-H(\omega_{B}).\end{array} (57)

of a state ωA1​…​An​B\,\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}\, is also used [44]. So, we will consider infinite-dimensional generalization of the quantity Sn(A1:…:An|B)\,S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B), having in mind that Sn(A1:…:An)\,S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}) is a partial case of Sn(A1:…:An|B)\,S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B) for trivial BB.

The conditional secrecy monotone SnS_{n} can be represented by conditioning (56) as follows

Sn(A1:…:An|B)ω=I(A1:A2…An|B)ω+I(A2:A3…An|A1B)ω+I(A3:A4…An|A1A2B)ω+…+I(An−1:An|A1…An−2B)ω.\begin{array}[]{c}S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega}=I(A_{1}\!:\!A_{2}...A_{n}|B)_{\omega}+\;I(A_{2}\!:\!A_{3}...A_{n}|A_{1}B)_{\omega}\\ \\ +I(A_{3}\!:\!A_{4}...A_{n}|A_{1}A_{2}B)_{\omega}+...+I(A_{n-1}\!:\!A_{n}|A_{1}...A_{n-2}B)_{\omega}.\end{array} (58)

Basic properties of the conditional mutual information show that the quantity Sn(A1:…:An|B)ωS_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega} is nonnegative and does not increase under local operations ΦA1:A1→A1,…,ΦAn:An→An\Phi_{A_{1}}:A_{1}\rightarrow A_{1},...,\Phi_{A_{n}}:A_{n}\rightarrow A_{n}, i.e.

Sn(A1:…:An|B)ω≥Sn(A1:…:An|B)ΦA1⊗…⊗ΦAn⊗IdB​(ω).S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega}\geq S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\Phi_{A_{1}}\otimes...\otimes\Phi_{A_{n}}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{B}(\omega)}. (59)

Formula (28) in this case has the form

Sn(A1:…:An|B)ω−Sn(A1:…:An)ω=(n−1)I(A1…An:B)ω−∑i=1nI(A1…Ai−1Ai+1…An:B)ω.\begin{array}[]{c}S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega}-S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n})_{\omega}=\displaystyle(n-1)I(A_{1}...A_{n}\!:\!B)_{\omega}\\ \displaystyle-\sum_{i=1}^{n}I(A_{1}...A_{i-1}A_{i+1}...A_{n}\!:\!B)_{\omega}.\end{array} (60)

Since (58) is valid with arbitrarily permuted indexes  1,…,n\,1,...,n\, in the right hand side, Remark 6.1 implies that Sn(A1:…:An|B)ωS_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega} is upper bounded by the value

2​min⁡∑i≠j1≤j≤n⁡H⁡(ωAi).2\min_{1\leq j\leq n}\sum_{i\neq j}H(\omega_{A_{i}}). (61)

By using representation (58) and the extended conditional mutual information described in Sect.6. one can define Sn(A1:…:An|B)ω\,S_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega} for any state of an infinite-dimensional system A1​…​An​BA_{1}...A_{n}B.

E) If n−1\,n-1\, subsystems, say A1,…,An−1A_{1},...,A_{n-1}, are finite-dimensional then Sn(A1:…:An|B)ωS_{n}(A_{1}\!:...:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega} is a continuous bounded function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An​B)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}) and

|Sn(A1:…:An|B)ω1−Sn(A1:…:An|B)ω2|≤2εC+2n(1+ε)h2(ε1+ε)|S_{n}(A_{1}\!:...:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega^{1}}-S_{n}(A_{1}\!:...:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega^{2}}|\leq 2\varepsilon C+2n(1+\varepsilon)h_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right)

for any ω1,ω2∈𝔖⁡(ℋA1​…​An​B)\,\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}B}) such that ε=12​‖ω1−ω2‖1<1\;\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{1}-\omega^{2}\|_{1}<1\,, where h2​(⋅)\,h_{2}(\cdot)\, is the binary entropy and C=logdimℋA1​…​An−1\,C=\log\dim\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n-1}}.

Proof. Assertion A follows from Theorem 6.1, Remark 6.1 and assertion C proved below.

Property (62) follows from Corollary6.1 and the second assertion of Corollary 6.1, i.e. limit relation (45), applied to each term in the right hand side of (58). This property and (45) make possible to prove assertion C via approximation by noting that it is valid for any state ωA1​…​An​B\omega_{A_{1}...A_{n}B} such that rank​ωAi<+∞\,\mathrm{rank}\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{i}}<+\infty for all ii and rank​ωB<+∞\,\mathrm{rank}\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{B}<+\infty.

Now, by using assertion C, the first part of assertion B can be proved by applying Corollary 6.1 to each term in the right hand side of (58) with appropriately permuted indexes  1,…,n\,1,...,n\, (and by using Lemmas 3 and 3).

The first part of assertion D follows from Corollary 6.1A applied to each term in the right hand side of (58) with appropriately permuted indexes  1,…,n\,1,...,n\,. The second part of assertion D follows from Proposition 4.3.

Assertion E follows from Proposition 3 and upper bound (61). □\square

Other properties (monotonicity under local conditioning, additivity, see [44]) of the extension Sn(A1:…:An|B)ωS_{n}(A_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}|B)_{\omega} defined in Proposition 7.2 can be derived from their validity in the finite-dimensional settings by using approximation property (62).

7.3 The gap I(A1A1′:…:AnAn′)−I(A1′:…:An′)I(A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}\!:\!...\!:\!A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n})-I(A^{\prime}_{1}\!:\!...\!:\!A^{\prime}_{n}) and the Wilde inequality

In construction of entanglement measures in a multipartite finite-dimensional quantum system A1​…​AnA_{1}...A_{n} the difference

ΔI(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)≐I(A1A1′:…:AnAn′)ω−I(A1′:…:An′)ω\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}})\doteq I(A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n})_{\omega}-I(A^{\prime}_{1}\!:\ldots:\!A^{\prime}_{n})_{\omega} (63)

between mutual informations of a state of the extended system A1​A1′​…​An​An′A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n} is used [45]. Basic properties of the quantum mutual information show that the gap Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) is nonnegative and does not increase under local operations ΦA1:A1→A1,…,ΦAn:An→An\Phi_{A_{1}}:A_{1}\rightarrow A_{1},...,\Phi_{A_{n}}:A_{n}\rightarrow A_{n}, i.e.

Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)≥Δ​I​(ΦA1⊗…⊗ΦAn⊗IdA1′​…​An′​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)).\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}})\geq\Delta I\left(\Phi_{A_{1}}\otimes...\otimes\Phi_{A_{n}}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{A_{1}^{\prime}...A_{n}^{\prime}}(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}})\right). (64)

Recently Wilde proved that

Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)≥14​n2​‖ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′−Φ1⊗…⊗Φn​(ωA1′​…​An′)‖12\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}})\geq\frac{1}{4n^{2}}\left\|\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}-\Phi_{1}\otimes...\otimes\Phi_{n}(\omega_{A^{\prime}_{1}...A^{\prime}_{n}})\right\|_{1}^{2} (65)

for particular recovery channels Φ1:A1′→A1​A1′,…,Φn:An′→An​An′\Phi_{1}:A^{\prime}_{1}\rightarrow A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1},...,\Phi_{n}:A^{\prime}_{n}\rightarrow A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n} [41].1818 18 In the recent paper [42] the version of this inequality not depending on n\,n\, is proved. This result shows that if the gap Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) is close to zero then the state ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}} can be approximately recovered from its marginal state ωA1′​…​An′\omega_{A^{\prime}_{1}...A^{\prime}_{n}} by the local recovery channels Φ1:A1′→A1​A1′,…,Φn:An′→An​An′\Phi_{1}:A^{\prime}_{1}\rightarrow A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1},...,\Phi_{n}:A^{\prime}_{n}\rightarrow A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}.

This result has several applications in quantum information theory [41]. It can be generalized to all states of infinite-dimensional quantum system A1​A1′​…​An​An′A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n} by constructing appropriate extension of the information gap Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) to the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) (see Corollary 7.3 below).

To construct this extension we will use the representation

Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)=I(A1:A′2…A′n|A′1)ω+∑i=2nI(Ai:A1…Ai−1A′1…A′i−1A′i+1…A′n|A′i)ω\begin{array}[]{rl}\displaystyle\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}})&=I(A_{1}\!:\!A^{\prime}_{2}...A^{\prime}_{n}|A^{\prime}_{1})_{\omega}\\ &\displaystyle+\sum_{i=2}^{n}I(A_{i}\!:\!A_{1}...A_{i-1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A^{\prime}_{i-1}A^{\prime}_{i+1}...A^{\prime}_{n}|A^{\prime}_{i})_{\omega}\end{array} (66)

valid for any state of a finite-dimensional system A1​A1′..An​An′A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}..A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n} [41, Lemma 1] and the extended conditional mutual information defined in Sect.6.

Proposition 8. A) The quantity Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\,\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) defined in (63) has a lower semicontinuous nonnegative extension to the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}\ldots A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) possessing property (64) and upper bounded by 2​∑i=1nH⁡(ωAi)2\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(\omega_{A_{i}}). For an arbitrary state ω∈𝔖⁡(ℋA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\,\omega\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}\ldots A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) the following weaker property is valid:

Δ​I​(ω)=limk→∞limk′→∞Δ​I​(ωk​k′),\Delta I(\omega)=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\lim_{k^{\prime}\rightarrow\infty}\Delta I(\omega^{kk^{\prime}}), (67)

where

ωk​k′=λ−1​Q​ω​Q,Q=PA1k⊗…⊗PAnk⊗PA1′k′⊗…⊗PAn′k′,λ=Tr​Q​ω,\omega^{kk^{\prime}}=\lambda^{-1}Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega\hskip 1.0ptQ,\quad Q=P^{k}_{A_{1}}\otimes\ldots\otimes P^{k}_{A_{n}}\otimes P^{k^{\prime}}_{A^{\prime}_{1}}\otimes\ldots\otimes P^{k^{\prime}}_{A^{\prime}_{n}},\quad\lambda=\mathrm{Tr}Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega,

{PAik}⊂𝔅⁡(ℋAi)\{P^{k}_{A_{i}}\}\subset\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{i}}) and {PAi′k′}⊂𝔅⁡(ℋAi′)\{P^{k^{\prime}}_{A^{\prime}_{i}}\}\subset\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A^{\prime}_{i}}) are any sequences of finite rank projectors strongly converging to the identity operators IAiI_{A_{i}} and IAi′I_{A^{\prime}_{i}}, i=1,n¯i=\overline{1,n}.
