E) If the subsystems A1,…,AnA_{1},...,A_{n} are finite-dimensional then Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\,\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) is a continuous bounded function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}\ldots A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) and

|Δ​I​(ω1)−Δ​I​(ω2)|≤2​ε​C+2​(n+1)​(1+ε)​h2​(ε1+ε)|\Delta I(\omega^{1})-\Delta I(\omega^{2})|\leq 2\varepsilon C+2(n+1)(1+\varepsilon)h_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right)

for any ω1,ω2∈𝔖⁡(ℋA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\,\omega^{1},\omega^{2}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}\ldots A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) such that ε=12​‖ω1−ω2‖1<1\;\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{1}-\omega^{2}\|_{1}<1\,, where h2​(⋅)\,h_{2}(\cdot)\, is the binary entropy and C=logdimℋA1​…​An\,C=\log\dim\mathcal{H}_{A_{1}...A_{n}}.

Proof. Assertion A is proved by using Theorem 6.1 and Remark 6.1.

Assertion B is proved by applying Corollaries 6.1 and 6.1 to each term in the right hand side of (66).

Assertion C is valid for any state ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}} such that rank​ωAi<+∞\,\mathrm{rank}\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A_{i}}<+\infty and rank​ωAi′<+∞\,\mathrm{rank}\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A^{\prime}_{i}}<+\infty for all ii by Lemma 1 in [41]. Its validity for arbitrary state can be shown via approximation by using properties (45) and (67).

Assertion D follows from Corollary 6.1A applied to each term in the right hand side of (66).

Assertion E follows from Proposition 3 and the upper bound for the quantity Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) mentioned in assertion A. □\square

Inequality (65) is proved in [41] by using the following two facts:

  • •

    the existence for any state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} of a finite-dimensional tripartite system of a channel Φ:B→B​C\Phi:B\rightarrow BC (the Fawzi-Renner recovery map) such that

    2−12I(A:C|B)ω≤F(ωA​B​C,IdA⊗Φ(ωA​B)),2^{-\frac{1}{2}I(A:C|B)_{\omega}}\leq F(\omega_{ABC},\mathrm{Id}_{A}\otimes\Phi(\omega_{AB})),

    where F⁡(ρ,σ)≐‖ρ​σ‖1F(\rho,\sigma)\doteq\|\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma}\|_{1} is the quantum fidelity [11];

  • •

    the validity of representation (66) with arbitrarily permuted indexes  1,…,n\,1,...,n\, in the right hand side which shows that for all i=1,n¯i=\overline{1,n} the following inequality holds

    ΔI(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)≥I(Ai:A1..Ai−1Ai+1..AnA1′..Ai−1′Ai+1′..An′|Ai′)ω.\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}})\geq I(A_{i}\!:\!A_{1}..A_{i-1}A_{i+1}..A_{n}A^{\prime}_{1}..A^{\prime}_{i-1}A^{\prime}_{i+1}..A^{\prime}_{n}|A^{\prime}_{i})_{\omega}.

The first fact is valid for all states of an infinite-dimensional tripartite system provided I(A:C|B)ω=Ie(A:C|B)ωI(A:C|B)_{\omega}=I_{\mathrm{e}}(A:C|B)_{\omega} – the extended conditional mutual information. For states with finite marginal entropies this is proved in [11], for arbitrary states this follows from Proposition 8.4 in Sect.8.4 below.

The second fact is valid for all states of an infinite-dimensional system A1​A1′​…​An​An′A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n} by Proposition 7.3C. So, by repeating the arguments from [41] one can prove inequality (65) for all states of an infinite-dimensional system A1​A1′​…​An​An′A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}.

Corollary 12. The Wilde inequality (65) is valid for all states of infinite-dimensional system A1​A1′​…​An​An′A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n} provided Δ​I​(ωA1​A1′​…​An​An′)\,\Delta I(\omega_{A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}...A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n}}) is the extension of the gap I(A1A1′:…:AnAn′)ω−I(A1′:…:An′)ω\,I(A_{1}A^{\prime}_{1}\!:\!...\!:\!A_{n}A^{\prime}_{n})_{\omega}-I(A^{\prime}_{1}\!:\!...\!:\!A^{\prime}_{n})_{\omega} described in Proposition 7.3.

8 Some applications

8.1 Triangle continuity relations for quantum channels

Let Φ:A→B\,\Phi:A\rightarrow B be a quantum channel – completely positive trace preserving linear map 𝔗⁡(ℋA)→𝔗⁡(ℋB)\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{A})\rightarrow\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{B}). Stinespring’s theorem implies the existence of a Hilbert space ℋE\mathcal{H}_{E} and of an isometry V:ℋA→ℋB⊗ℋEV:\mathcal{H}_{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_{B}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{E} such that

Φ⁡(ρ)=TrE​V​ρ​V∗,ρ∈𝔗⁡(ℋA).\Phi(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}_{E}V\rho V^{*},\quad\rho\in\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{A}).

The quantum channel

𝔗⁡(ℋA)∋ρ↦Φ^​(ρ)=TrB​V​ρ​V∗∈𝔗⁡(ℋE)\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{A})\ni\rho\mapsto\widehat{\Phi}(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}_{B}V\rho V^{*}\in\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{E}) (68)

is called complementary to the channel Φ\Phi [16, Ch.6].

It is well known that for a finite-dimensional channel Φ\,\Phi and a state ρ\rho in 𝔖⁡(ℋA)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) the input entropy H⁡(ρ)H(\rho), the output entropy H⁡(Φ⁡(ρ))H(\Phi(\rho)) and the entropy exchange H⁡(Φ,ρ)≐H⁡(Φ^​(ρ))H(\Phi,\rho)\doteq H(\widehat{\Phi}(\rho)) denoted respectively HΦ​(ρ)H_{\Phi}(\rho) and HΦ^​(ρ)H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho) satisfy the ”triangle inequalities”:

|HΦ​(ρ)−HΦ^​(ρ)|≤H⁡(ρ),|HΦ(ρ)−H(ρ)|≤HΦ^(ρ),|HΦ^(ρ)−H(ρ)|≤HΦ(ρ).\begin{array}[]{c}\left|H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho)\right|\leq H(\rho),\\ \\ \left|H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H(\rho)\right|\leq H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho),\quad\left|H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho)-H(\rho)\right|\leq H_{\Phi}(\rho).\end{array} (69)

The quantity Ic​(Φ,ρ)≐HΦ​(ρ)−HΦ^​(ρ)I_{c}(\Phi,\rho)\doteq H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho) called coherent information of a channel Φ\Phi at a state ρ\rho is an important characteristic of a quantum channel related to its quantum capacity [16, 33].

The quantity E​G​(Φ,ρ)≐HΦ​(ρ)−H⁡(ρ)EG(\Phi,\rho)\doteq H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H(\rho) called entropy gain of a channel Φ\Phi at a state ρ\rho is a convex function of ρ\rho also used in analysis of information properties of a quantum channel [2, 18].

If Φ\Phi is an infinite-dimensional quantum channel, then inequalities (69) also hold provided all the terms are finite. Moreover, if we use the extension of the coherent information Ic​(Φ,ρ)=HΦ​(ρ)−HΦ^​(ρ)I_{c}(\Phi,\rho)=H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho) to the set {ρ∈𝔖⁡(ℋA)|H⁡(ρ)<+∞}\{\rho\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A})\,|\,H(\rho)<+\infty\} given by the formula1919 19 The reasonability of this extension is shown in [20].

Ic(Φ,ρ)=H(Φ⊗IdR(|φρ⟩⟨φρ|)∥Φ(ρ)⊗ϱ)−H(ρ),I_{c}(\Phi,\rho)=H\left(\Phi\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{R}(|\varphi_{\rho}\rangle\langle\varphi_{\rho}|)\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\Phi(\rho)\otimes\varrho\hskip 1.0pt\right)-H(\rho), (70)

where |φρ⟩|\varphi_{\rho}\rangle is a purification of the state ρ\rho in ℋA⊗ℋR\mathcal{H}_{A}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{R} and ϱ=TrA​|φρ⟩​⟨φρ|\varrho=\mathrm{Tr}_{A}|\varphi_{\rho}\rangle\langle\varphi_{\rho}|, then upper bound (19) implies that the first inequality in (69) becomes valid for arbitrary state ρ\rho (with possible value +∞+\infty in the both sides).

The quantities E​G​(Φ,ρ)=HΦ​(ρ)−H⁡(ρ)EG(\Phi,\rho)=H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H(\rho) and E​G​(Φ^,ρ)=HΦ^​(ρ)−H⁡(ρ)EG(\widehat{\Phi},\rho)=H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho)-H(\rho) can be extended respectively by the formulae

EG(Φ,ρ)=H(VρV∗∥Φ(ρ)⊗Φ^(ρ))−HΦ^(ρ)EG(\Phi,\rho)=H\left(V\rho V^{*}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\Phi(\rho)\otimes\widehat{\Phi}(\rho)\right)-H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho) (71)

and

EG(Φ^,ρ)=H(VρV∗∥Φ(ρ)⊗Φ^(ρ))−HΦ(ρ)EG(\widehat{\Phi},\rho)=H\left(V\rho V^{*}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\Phi(\rho)\otimes\widehat{\Phi}(\rho)\right)-H_{\Phi}(\rho) (72)

to the sets {ρ∈𝔖⁡(ℋA)|HΦ^​(ρ)<+∞}\{\rho\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A})\,|\,H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho)<+\infty\} and {ρ∈𝔖⁡(ℋA)|HΦ​(ρ)<+∞}\{\rho\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A})\,|\,H_{\Phi}(\rho)<+\infty\}, where VV is any Stinespring isometry for Φ\Phi and Φ^\widehat{\Phi} is the version of complementary channel corresponding to this isometry via (68). The right hand sides of (71) and (72) can be written respectively as −He​(E|B)V​ρ​V∗-H_{\mathrm{e}}(E|B)_{V\rho V^{*}} and −He​(B|E)V​ρ​V∗-H_{\mathrm{e}}(B|E)_{V\rho V^{*}}, where He​(A|B)H_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B) is the extended quantum conditional entropy proposed in [27] and described in Sec.5. So, the concavity of He​(A|B)H_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B) implies the convexity of E​G​(Φ,ρ)EG(\Phi,\rho) and of E​G​(Φ^,ρ)EG(\widehat{\Phi},\rho) defined by (71) and (72) as functions of ρ\rho. The upper bound (19) shows that

|E​G​(Φ,ρ)|≤HΦ^​(ρ)and|E​G​(Φ^,ρ)|≤HΦ​(ρ).|EG(\Phi,\rho)|\leq H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho)\quad\textrm{and}\quad|EG(\widehat{\Phi},\rho)|\leq H_{\Phi}(\rho).

So, the second and the third inequalities in (69) are also valid for arbitrary state ρ\rho (with possible value +∞+\infty in the both sides) provided the values HΦ​(ρ)−H​(ρ)H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H(\rho) and HΦ^​(ρ)−H​(ρ)H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho)-H(\rho) are defined respectively by formulae (71) and (72).

Theorem 4.1A makes possible to show that continuity of one of the functions H⁡(ρ),HΦ​(ρ),HΦ^​(ρ)H(\rho),H_{\Phi}(\rho),H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho) implies continuity of the difference between two others.

Proposition 9. Let Φ:A→B\,\Phi:A\rightarrow B be a quantum channel and Φ^:A→E\;\widehat{\Phi}:A\rightarrow E\, its complementary channel. Then

  1. A)

    local continuity of H⁡(ρ)\,H(\rho) implies local continuity of the coherent information Ic​(Φ,ρ)=[HΦ​(ρ)−HΦ^​(ρ)]\,I_{c}(\Phi,\rho)=[H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho)]\, defined by formula (70);

  2. B)

    local continuity of HΦ^​(ρ)\,H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho) implies local continuity of the entropy gain E​G​(Φ,ρ)=[HΦ​(ρ)−H⁡(ρ)]\,EG(\Phi,\rho)=[H_{\Phi}(\rho)-H(\rho)]\, defined by formula (71);

  3. C)

    local continuity of HΦ​(ρ)\,H_{\Phi}(\rho) implies local continuity of the entropy gain E​G​(Φ^,ρ)=[HΦ^​(ρ)−H⁡(ρ)]\,EG(\widehat{\Phi},\rho)=[H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho)-H(\rho)]\, defined by formula (72).

While triangle inequalities (69) show existence of a triangle with sides of length H⁡(ρ),HΦ​(ρ),HΦ^​(ρ)H(\rho),H_{\Phi}(\rho),H_{\widehat{\Phi}}(\rho), Proposition 8.1 states that a small deformation of any side of this triangle leads to a small deformation of the difference between the other sides (despite possible large deformation of each of these sides).

Proof. Assertions B and C directly follow from Theorem 4.1A. Assertion A is also derived from Theorem 4.1A by using Lemma 2 and by noting that H⁡(ϱ)=H⁡(ρ)H(\varrho)=H(\rho) for the state ϱ\varrho in (70). □\square

Since E​G​(Φ,ρ)=−He​(E|B)V​ρ​V∗EG(\Phi,\rho)=-H_{\mathrm{e}}(E|B)_{V\rho V^{*}}, by applying Corollary 5 one can strengthen assertion B of Proposition 8.1 in the case dimℋE=k<+∞\dim\mathcal{H}_{E}=k<+\infty.

Corollary 13. If Φ:A→B\,\Phi:A\rightarrow B is a quantum channel with finite Choi rank k\,k\, then the entropy gain (71) is a continuous bounded function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) and

|E​G​(Φ,ρ1)−E​G​(Φ,ρ2)|≤2​ε​log⁡k+(1+ε)​h2​(ε1+ε)|EG(\Phi,\rho_{1})-EG(\Phi,\rho_{2})|\leq 2\varepsilon\log k+(1+\varepsilon)h_{2}\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right)

for any ρ1,ρ2∈𝔖⁡(ℋA)\,\rho_{1},\rho_{2}\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) such that ε=12​‖ρ1−ρ2‖1<1\,\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\|\hskip 1.0pt\rho_{1}-\rho_{2}\|_{1}<1, where h2​(⋅)h_{2}(\cdot) is the binary entropy.

By applying Corollary 4.1 and by noting that dimℋR=dimℋA\dim\mathcal{H}_{R}=\dim\mathcal{H}_{A} one can obtain continuity bounds for the coherent information (70) and for the quantum mutual information (74) in the case dimℋA<+∞\dim\mathcal{H}_{A}<+\infty.

8.2 Continuity conditions for the
functions (Φ,ρ)↦I⁡(Φ,ρ)(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I(\Phi,\rho) and (Φ,ρ)↦Ic​(Φ,ρ)(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I_{c}(\Phi,\rho)

The quantum mutual information is an important characteristic of a quantum channel related to its entanglement-assisted classical capacity [1, 5, 16, 33]. For a finite-dimensional channel Φ:A→B\Phi:A\rightarrow B it can be defined by the formula

I⁡(Φ,ρ)=H⁡(ρ)+H⁡(Φ⁡(ρ))−H⁡(Φ^​(ρ)).I(\Phi,\rho)=H(\rho)+H(\Phi(\rho))-H(\widehat{\Phi}(\rho)). (73)

In infinite dimensions this definition may contain the uncertainty "​∞−∞​""\infty-\infty", but it can be modified to avoid this problem as follows

I(Φ,ρ)=H(Φ⊗IdR(|φρ⟩⟨φρ|)∥Φ(ρ)⊗ϱ),I(\Phi,\rho)=H\left(\Phi\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{R}(|\varphi_{\rho}\rangle\langle\varphi_{\rho}|)\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\Phi(\rho)\otimes\varrho\hskip 1.0pt\right), (74)

where |φρ⟩|\varphi_{\rho}\rangle is a purification of the state ρ\rho in ℋA⊗ℋR\mathcal{H}_{A}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{R} and ϱ=TrA​|φρ⟩​⟨φρ|\varrho=\mathrm{Tr}_{A}|\varphi_{\rho}\rangle\langle\varphi_{\rho}|. For an arbitrary quantum channel Φ\Phi the nonnegative function ρ↦I⁡(Φ,ρ)\rho\mapsto I(\Phi,\rho) defined by (74) is concave and lower semicontinuous on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) [20].

In study of the entanglement-assisted classical capacity of an infinite-dimensional channel, in particular, in the analysis of its continuity as a function of a channel (which can be interpreted as a robustness or stability of the capacity with respect to perturbation of a channel) it is necessary to explore continuity properties of the quantum mutual information I⁡(Φ,ρ)I(\Phi,\rho) with respect to simultaneous variation of Φ\Phi and ρ\rho. This means that we have to consider I⁡(Φ,ρ)I(\Phi,\rho) as a function of a pair (Φ,ρ)(\Phi,\rho), i.e. as a function on the Cartesian product of the set 𝔉A​B\mathfrak{F}_{AB} of all quantum channels from AA to BB equipped with appropriate topology (type of convergence) and the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) of input states.

Since a quantum channel Φ\Phi is a completely bounded map, the set 𝔉A​B\mathfrak{F}_{AB} is typically equipped with the norm of complete boundedness [34], which can be defined as the upper bound of the operator norms of the maps Φ⊗Idℂn\Phi\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^{n}}, n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N}. In infinite dimensions along with the topology induced by the norm of complete boundedness one can consider weaker topologies on the set of quantum channels, in particular, the strong convergence topology generated by the strong operator topology on the set of all linear bounded operators between the Banach spaces 𝔗⁡(ℋA)\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) and 𝔗⁡(ℋB)\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{B}) [19]. The strong convergence of a sequence {Φn}⊂𝔉A​B\{\Phi_{n}\}\subset\mathfrak{F}_{AB} to a quantum channel Φ0∈𝔉A​B\Phi_{0}\in\mathfrak{F}_{AB} means that

limn→+∞Φn​(ρ)=Φ0​(ρ)∀ρ∈𝔖⁡(ℋA).\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}\Phi_{n}(\rho)=\Phi_{0}(\rho)\quad\forall\rho\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}).

The use of the strong convergence topology in infinite dimensions seems preferable by the following reason. It is shown in [25] that closeness of two quantum channels in the norm of complete boundedness means, roughly speaking, the operator norm closeness of the corresponding Stinespring isometries. So, if we use the norm of complete boundedness then we take into account only such perturbations of a channel that corresponds to uniform deformations of the Stinespring isometry (i.e. deformations with small operator norm). Physically, it seems reasonable to consider the wider class of perturbations of a channel including the perturbations corresponding to deformations of the Stinespring isometry in the strong operator topology.

Thus, we will assume in what follows that 𝔉A​B\mathfrak{F}_{AB} is the set all channels Φ:A→B\,\Phi:A\rightarrow B equipped with the strong convergence topology. By separability of the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA)\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) the strong convergence topology on the set 𝔉A​B\mathfrak{F}_{AB} is metrizable (can be induced by some metric). Note also that it is the strong convergence topology that makes the set 𝔉A​B\mathfrak{F}_{AB} to be topologically isomorphic to a subset of states of a composite system (generalized Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism) [19, Proposition 3].

By using Theorem 4.1 one can substantially amplify the continuity condition for the function (Φ,ρ)↦I⁡(Φ,ρ)\,(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I(\Phi,\rho) obtained in [20, Proposition 5].

Proposition 10. A) Continuity of H⁡(ρ)\,H(\rho) on a set 𝒜⊂𝔖⁡(ℋA)\mathcal{A}\subset\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) implies continuity of the function (Φ,ρ)↦I⁡(Φ,ρ)\;(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I(\Phi,\rho)\, on the set 𝔉A​B×𝒜\,\mathfrak{F}_{AB}\times\mathcal{A}.

B) Local continuity of the function (Φ,ρ)↦H⁡(Φ⁡(ρ))\,(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto H(\Phi(\rho)) implies local continuity of the function (Φ,ρ)↦I⁡(Φ,ρ)\,(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I(\Phi,\rho).

C) Local continuity of the function (Φ,ρ)↦I⁡(Φ,ρ)\,(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I(\Phi,\rho) implies local continuity of the function (Φ,ρ)↦I⁡(Ψ∘Φ,ρ)\,(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I(\Psi\circ\Phi,\rho) for any channel Ψ:B→C\,\Psi:B\rightarrow C.

Assertion A of Proposition 8.2 states that

limn→∞H⁡(ρn)=H⁡(ρ0)<+∞⇒limn→∞I⁡(Φn,ρn)=I⁡(Φ0,ρ0)<+∞\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}H(\rho_{n})=H(\rho_{0})<+\infty\;\;\Rightarrow\;\;\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}I(\Phi_{n},\rho_{n})=I(\Phi_{0},\rho_{0})<+\infty (75)

where ρ0=limn→∞ρn\rho_{0}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\rho_{n}, for arbitrary sequence {Φn}\{\Phi_{n}\} of channels strongly converging to a channel Φ0\Phi_{0}. In contrast to Proposition 5 in [20] the existence of a sequence {Φ^n}\{\widehat{\Phi}_{n}\} converging to the channel Φ^0\widehat{\Phi}_{0} is not required in (75).

Assertions B and C can be formulated as the implications:

limn→∞H⁡(Φn​(ρn))=H⁡(Φ0​(ρ0))<+∞⇒limn→∞I⁡(Φn,ρn)=I⁡(Φ0,ρ0)<+∞\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}H(\Phi_{n}(\rho_{n}))=H(\Phi_{0}(\rho_{0}))<+\infty\;\Rightarrow\;\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}I(\Phi_{n},\rho_{n})=I(\Phi_{0},\rho_{0})<+\infty

and

limn→∞I⁡(Φn,ρn)=I⁡(Φ0,ρ0)<+∞⇒limn→∞I⁡(Ψ∘Φn,ρn)=I⁡(Ψ∘Φ0,ρ0)<+∞\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\!I(\Phi_{n},\rho_{n})=\!I(\Phi_{0},\rho_{0})<+\infty\;\Rightarrow\;\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\!I(\Psi\circ\Phi_{n},\rho_{n})=\!I(\Psi\circ\Phi_{0},\rho_{0})<+\infty

valid for sequences {ρn}⊂𝔖⁡(ℋA)\{\rho_{n}\}\subset\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) and {Φn}⊂𝔉A​B\{\Phi_{n}\}\subset\mathfrak{F}_{AB} converging respectively to a state ρ0\rho_{0} and to a channel Φ0\Phi_{0} and arbitrary channel Ψ∈𝔉B​C\Psi\in\mathfrak{F}_{BC}.

Proof. Since the strong convergence of a sequence {Φn}\{\Phi_{n}\} to a channel Φ0\Phi_{0} implies the strong convergence of the sequence {Φn⊗IdR}\{\Phi_{n}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{R}\} to the channel Φ0⊗IdR\Phi_{0}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{R} [19], assertions A and B follow from Theorem 4.1A and Lemma 2 (since H⁡(ϱ)=H⁡(ρ)H(\varrho)=H(\rho) for the state ϱ\varrho in (74)) while assertion C follows from Theorem 4.1B. □\square

Proposition 8.2A gives a continuity condition for the coherent information Ic​(Φ,ρ)I_{c}(\Phi,\rho) defined by formula (70) which means Ic​(Φ,ρ)=I⁡(Φ,ρ)−H⁡(ρ)\,I_{c}(\Phi,\rho)=I(\Phi,\rho)-H(\rho).

Corollary 14. Continuity of H⁡(ρ)\,H(\rho) on a set 𝒜⊂𝔖⁡(ℋA)\mathcal{A}\subset\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) implies continuity of the function (Φ,ρ)↦Ic​(Φ,ρ)\;(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I_{c}(\Phi,\rho)\, on the set 𝔉A​B×𝒜\,\mathfrak{F}_{AB}\times\mathcal{A}.

Corollary 8.2 states that implication (75) holds with Ic​(Φ,ρ)I_{c}(\Phi,\rho) instead of I⁡(Φ,ρ)I(\Phi,\rho), it can be considered as a generalized version of Proposition 8.1A.

It is easy to see that the analog of Proposition 8.2B is not valid for the function (Φ,ρ)↦Ic​(Φ,ρ)(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I_{c}(\Phi,\rho).

8.3 On continuity of the entanglement assisted classical capacity as a function of channel

In this section we substantially strengthen the conditions for continuity of the entanglement-assisted classical capacity of an infinite-dimensional quantum channel with linear constraint (as a function of a channel) obtained in [21].2020 20 The importance of studying continuity properties of quantum channel capacities is discussed in [28, 19, 21]. It is explained, briefly speaking, by unavoidable perturbations of a channel used for information transmission.

A rate of transmission of classical information over a quantum channel can be increased by using an entangled state as an additional resource. A detailed description of the corresponding protocol can be found in [16, 33]. The ultimate rate of information transmission by this protocol is called entanglement-assisted classical capacity of a quantum channel.

If Φ:A→B\Phi:A\rightarrow B is a finite-dimensional quantum channel then the Bennett-Shor-Smolin-Thaplyal (BSST) theorem [5] gives the following expression for its entanglement-assisted classical capacity

Cea​(Φ)=supρ∈𝔖⁡(ℋA)I⁡(Φ,ρ),C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi)=\sup_{\rho\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A})}I(\Phi,\rho),

where I⁡(Φ,ρ)I(\Phi,\rho) is the quantum mutual information defined by (73).

Continuity if this capacity as a function of a channel directly follows from continuity of the function (Φ,ρ)↦I⁡(Φ,ρ)(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I(\Phi,\rho) and compactness of the space of input states [28].

If Φ\Phi is an infinite-dimensional quantum channel then we have to impose constraint on states used for coding information, typically linear constraint determined by the inequality Tr​F​ρ≤E\mathrm{Tr}F\rho\leq E, where FF is a positive operator and E>0E>0. An operational definition of the entanglement-assisted classical capacity Cea​(Φ,F,E)C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi,F,E) of an infinite-dimensional quantum channel Φ\Phi with the above linear constraint is given in [17], where the generalization of the BSST theorem is proved under special restrictions on the channel Φ\Phi and on the constraint operator FF. A general version of the BSST theorem for infinite-dimensional channel with linear constraints without any simplifying restrictions is proved in [21] (by using the extended quantum conditional entropy He​(A|B)H_{\mathrm{e}}(A|B) proposed in [27] and described in Sec.5), it states that

Cea​(Φ,F,E)=supTr​F​ρ≤EI⁡(Φ,ρ)≤+∞C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi,F,E)=\sup_{\mathrm{Tr}F\rho\leq E}I(\Phi,\rho)\leq+\infty (76)

for arbitrary channel Φ\,\Phi and arbitrary constraint operator FF, where I⁡(Φ,ρ)I(\Phi,\rho) is the quantum mutual information defined by formula (74).

By noting that the function (Φ,ρ)↦I⁡(Φ,ρ)(\Phi,\rho)\mapsto I(\Phi,\rho) is lower semicontinuous on 𝔉A​B×𝔖⁡(ℋA)\mathfrak{F}_{AB}\times\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) (see [20]) it is easy to show that the function Φ↦Cea​(Φ,F,E)\Phi\mapsto C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi,F,E) is lower semicontinuous on 𝔉A​B\mathfrak{F}_{AB}, i.e.

lim infn→+∞Cea​(Φn,F,E)≥Cea​(Φ0,F,E)(≤+∞)\liminf_{n\rightarrow+\infty}C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{n},F,E)\geq C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{0},F,E)\;\;(\leq+\infty)

for any sequence {Φn}\{\Phi_{n}\} of channels strongly converging to a channel Φ0\Phi_{0}. But this function is not continuous in general (see Example 8.3 below).

Proposition 8.2A implies the following sufficient condition for global continuity of the function Φ↦Cea​(Φ,F,E)\Phi\mapsto C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi,F,E).

Proposition 11. Let 𝒦F,E\mathcal{K}_{F,E} be the set of input states ρ\rho such that Tr​F​ρ≤E\,\mathrm{Tr}F\rho\leq E

If H⁡(ρ)\,H(\rho) is continuous on 𝒦F,E\,\mathcal{K}_{F,E} then the function Φ↦Cea​(Φ,F,E)\,\Phi\mapsto C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi,F,E)\, is continuous on the set 𝔉A​B\,\mathfrak{F}_{AB} of all channels (and upper bounded by supρ∈𝒦F,E2​H​(ρ)\displaystyle\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal{K}_{F,E}}\!\!2H(\rho)).

The assumption of continuity of H⁡(ρ)\,H(\rho) on 𝒦F,E\,\mathcal{K}_{F,E} holds for any E>0E>0 if the operator FF satisfies the condition Tr​exp⁡(−λ​F)<+∞\mathrm{Tr}\exp(-\lambda F)<+\infty for all λ>0\lambda>0 [40]. This condition is valid if F=R⊤​ϵ​RF=R^{\top}\epsilon R – Hamiltonian of a many-mode Bosonic quantum system, where ϵ\epsilon is a nondegenerate energy matrix and RR are the canonical variables of the system (see details in [16, Ch.12]). In this case Cea​(Φ,F,E)C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi,F,E) is the entanglement-assisted classical capacity of a channel Φ\Phi under the condition that the mean energy of states used for coding information is ≤E\leq E. Proposition 8.3 implies the following observation.

Corollary 15. Let F=R⊤​ϵ​R\,F=R^{\top}\epsilon R be a Hamiltonian of a many-mode Bosonic quantum system AA and E>0E>0. The function Φ↦Cea​(Φ,F,E)\,\Phi\mapsto C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi,F,E)\, is continuous on the set 𝔉A​B\,\mathfrak{F}_{AB} of all channels from the system A to any system B.

This corollary shows that the entanglement-assisted classical capacity of a Bosonic Gaussian channel with energy constraint is continuously varies under any perturbations of this channel.

Proof of Proposition 8.3. Since the set 𝒦F,E\mathcal{K}_{F,E} is closed and convex, the continuity of the concave function H⁡(ρ)\,H(\rho) on 𝒦F,E\mathcal{K}_{F,E} implies boundedness of this function on 𝒦F,E\mathcal{K}_{F,E}.2121 21 If for each nn there is a state ρn∈𝒦F,E\rho_{n}\in\mathcal{K}_{F,E} such that H⁡(ρn)≥2nH(\rho_{n})\geq 2^{n} then ∑n=1+∞2−n​ρn∈𝒦F,E\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}2^{-n}\rho_{n}\in\mathcal{K}_{F,E} and H⁡(∑n=1+∞2−n​ρn)≥∑n=1+∞2−n​H​(ρn)=+∞H\left(\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}2^{-n}\rho_{n}\right)\geq\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}2^{-n}H\left(\rho_{n}\right)=+\infty contradicting to the continuity of HH. So, by Corollary 5 in [36] the set 𝒦F,E\mathcal{K}_{F,E} is compact.

Since the function Φ↦Cea​(Φ,F,E)\,\Phi\mapsto C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi,F,E)\, is lower semicontinuous on the set 𝔉A​B\,\mathfrak{F}_{AB} it suffices to show that it is finite and upper semicontinuous.

Assume that there exists a sequence {Φn}\{\Phi_{n}\} of channels in 𝔉A​B\mathfrak{F}_{AB} strongly converging to a channel Φ0\Phi_{0} such that

limn→+∞Cea​(Φn,F,E)≥Cea​(Φ0,F,E)+ε\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{n},F,E)\geq C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{0},F,E)+\varepsilon (77)

for some ε>0\varepsilon>0. It follows from (76) that for each nn there is a state ρn∈𝒦F,E\rho_{n}\in\mathcal{K}_{F,E} such that

Cea​(Φn,F,E)<I⁡(Φn,ρn)+ε/2.C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{n},F,E)<I(\Phi_{n},\rho_{n})+\varepsilon/2.

By compactness of the set 𝒦F,E\mathcal{K}_{F,E} we may assume (by passing to a subsequence) that the sequence {ρn}\{\rho_{n}\} converges to a particular state ρ0∈𝒦F,E\rho_{0}\in\mathcal{K}_{F,E}. Proposition 8.2A implies

limn→+∞I⁡(Φn,ρn)=I⁡(Φ0,ρ0).\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}I(\Phi_{n},\rho_{n})=I(\Phi_{0},\rho_{0}).

Since (76) shows that Cea​(Φ0,F,E)≥I⁡(Φ0,ρ0)C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{0},F,E)\geq I(\Phi_{0},\rho_{0}), this contradicts to (77). □\square

By using Proposition 8.2B and the same arguments one can prove the following ”local” continuity condition.

Proposition 12. If 𝒦F,E={ρ∈𝔖⁡(ℋA)|Tr​F​ρ≤E}\,\mathcal{K}_{F,E}=\{\rho\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A})\,|\,\mathrm{Tr}F\rho\leq E\} is a compact set and {Φn}\{\Phi_{n}\} is a sequence of channels strongly converging to a channel Φ0\Phi_{0} such that limn→+∞H⁡(Φn​(ρn))=H⁡(Φ0​(ρ0))<+∞\displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}H(\Phi_{n}(\rho_{n}))=H(\Phi_{0}(\rho_{0}))<+\infty for any sequence {ρn}⊂𝒦F,E\{\rho_{n}\}\subset\mathcal{K}_{F,E} converging to a state ρ0\rho_{0} then

limn→+∞Cea​(Φn,F,E)=Cea​(Φ0,F,E)<+∞.\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{n},F,E)=C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{0},F,E)<+\infty. (78)

Remark 8. The same continuity condition holds for the Holevo capacity of an infinite-dimensional channel with linear constraints [19, Proposition 7].

The following example shows that compactness of the set 𝒦F,E\mathcal{K}_{F,E} and continuity of the output entropies of all the channels Φn\Phi_{n} do not imply (78).

Example 2. Let {|k⟩}k≥0\{|k\rangle\}_{k\geq 0} be an orthonormal basic in a separable Hilbert space ℋA=ℋB\mathcal{H}_{A}=\mathcal{H}_{B} and Pn=∑k=1n|k⟩​⟨k|P_{n}=\sum_{k=1}^{n}|k\rangle\langle k| be a projector of rank nn. Consider the sequence of channels

Φn​(ρ)=[Tr⁡(IA−qn​Pn)​ρ]​|0⟩​⟨0|+qn​Pn​ρ​Pn\Phi_{n}(\rho)=[\mathrm{Tr}(I_{A}-q_{n}P_{n})\rho\hskip 1.0pt]|0\rangle\langle 0|+q_{n}P_{n}\rho P_{n}

with finite-dimensional output space, where {qn}\{q_{n}\} is a sequence of positive numbers specified below.

Let F=∑k=0+∞log⁡(log⁡(k+3))​|k⟩​⟨k|F=\sum_{k=0}^{+\infty}\log(\log(k+3))|k\rangle\langle k| be a positive operator. By the Lemma in [17] the corresponding set 𝒦F,E\mathcal{K}_{F,E} is compact. Since Tr​exp⁡(−λ​F)=+∞\mathrm{Tr}\exp(-\lambda F)=+\infty for any λ>0\lambda>0, Proposition 1a in [36] and its proof imply the existence of a sequence {ρn}⊂𝒦F,E\{\rho_{n}\}\subset\mathcal{K}_{F,E} such that ρn=Pn​ρn​Pn\rho_{n}=P_{n}\rho_{n}P_{n} and limn→∞H⁡(ρn)=+∞\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}H(\rho_{n})=+\infty.

It is easy to show that I⁡(Φn,ρn)≥2​qn​H​(Pn​ρn​Pn)=2​qn​H​(ρn)I(\Phi_{n},\rho_{n})\geq 2q_{n}H(P_{n}\rho_{n}P_{n})=2q_{n}H(\rho_{n}). Since {ρn}⊂𝒦F,E\{\rho_{n}\}\subset\mathcal{K}_{F,E}, this implies Cea​(Φn,F,E)≥2​qn​H​(ρn)C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{n},F,E)\geq 2q_{n}H(\rho_{n}). So, for any sequence {qn}\{q_{n}\} such that limn→∞qn=0\,\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}q_{n}=0\, and limn→∞qn​H​(ρn)=C>0\,\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}q_{n}H(\rho_{n})=C>0 we have

lim infn→+∞Cea​(Φn,F,E)≥2​C,\liminf_{n\rightarrow+\infty}C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{n},F,E)\geq 2C,

while the sequence {Φn}\{\Phi_{n}\} strongly converges to the completely depolarizing channel Φ0​(ρ)=[Tr​ρ]​|0⟩​⟨0|\Phi_{0}(\rho)=[\mathrm{Tr}\rho]|0\rangle\langle 0| for which Cea​(Φ0,F,E)=0C_{\mathrm{ea}}(\Phi_{0},F,E)=0.

8.4 On existence of the Fawzi-Renner recovery channel for arbitrary tripartite state

The fundamental strong subadditivity property of the von Neumann entropy, which means the nonnegativity of I(A:C|B)ω\,I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}, was recently specified by Fawzi and Renner who proved in [11] that for any state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} there exists a recovery channel Φ:B→B​C\Phi:B\rightarrow BC such that

2−12I(A:C|B)ω≤F(ωA​B​C,IdA⊗Φ(ωA​B))2^{-\frac{1}{2}I(A:C|B)_{\omega}}\leq F(\omega_{ABC},\mathrm{Id}_{A}\otimes\Phi(\omega_{AB})) (79)

where F⁡(ρ,σ)≐‖ρ​σ‖1F(\rho,\sigma)\doteq\|\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma}\|_{1} is the quantum fidelity between states ρ\rho and σ\sigma.2222 22 Recently it was shown that the recovery channel Φ:B→B​C\Phi:B\rightarrow BC satisfying (79) can be chosen independently of AA [38]. This result can be considered as a ε\varepsilon-version of the well-known characterization of a state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} for which I(A:C|B)ω=0I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=0 as a Markov chain (i.e. as a state reconstructed from its marginal state ωA​B\omega_{AB} by a channel IdA⊗Φ\mathrm{Id}_{A}\otimes\Phi). It has several important applications in quantum information theory [11, 41].

The existence of a channel Φ\Phi satisfying (79) is proved in [11] in finite-dimensional settings by quasi-explicit construction. Then, by using approximation technic, this result is extended in [11, 38] to a state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} of infinite-dimensional system assuming that I(A:C|B)ω=H(A|B)ω−H(A|BC)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=H(A|B)_{\omega}-H(A|BC)_{\omega}, i.e. assuming that the marginal entropies of ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} are finite.

It is also shown in Remark 5.3 in [11] that in finite dimensions a channel Φ:B→B​C\Phi:B\rightarrow BC satisfying (79) can be chosen in such a way that

[Φ⁡(ωB)]B=ωBand[Φ⁡(ωB)]C=ωC,[\Phi(\omega_{B})]_{B}=\omega_{B}\quad\textrm{and}\quad[\Phi(\omega_{B})]_{C}=\omega_{C}, (80)

i.e. a recovery channel Φ\Phi may exactly reproduce the marginal states.2323 23 In Remark 5.3 in [11] the existence of a quantum operation Φ′\Phi^{\prime} satisfying (79) such that [Φ′​(ωB)]B≤ωB[\Phi^{\prime}(\omega_{B})]_{B}\leq\omega_{B} and [Φ′​(ωB)]C≤ωC[\Phi^{\prime}(\omega_{B})]_{C}\leq\omega_{C} is shown. A quantum channels Φ\Phi satisfying (79) and (80) can be obtained via Φ′\Phi^{\prime} as follows Φ⁡(ρ)=Φ′​(ρ)+[Tr​ρ−Tr​Φ′​(ρ)]​σ\Phi(\rho)=\Phi^{\prime}(\rho)+[\mathrm{Tr}\rho-\mathrm{Tr}\Phi^{\prime}(\rho)]\hskip 1.0pt\sigma, where σ\sigma is the normalized positive operator (ωB−[Φ′​(ωB)]B)⊗(ωC−[Φ′​(ωB)]C)(\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{B}-[\hskip 1.0pt\Phi^{\prime}(\omega_{B})]_{B})\otimes(\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{C}-[\hskip 1.0pt\Phi^{\prime}(\omega_{B})]_{C}).

The properties of the extended conditional mutual information (described in Section 6) make possible to show the existence of a recovery channel satisfying (80) for all states of infinite-dimensional tripartite system starting with the above-mentioned finite-dimensional result.

Proposition 13. (ID-version of Remark 5.3 in [11]) For arbitrary state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} of infinite-dimensional tripartite system there exists a channel Φ:B→B​C\,\Phi:B\rightarrow BC satisfying (79) and (80) provided I(A:C|B)ω\,I(A:C|B)_{\omega} is the extended conditional mutual information (described in Theorem 6.1).

We will use the following corollary of the compactness criterion for families of quantum operations in the strong convergence topology [19, Corollary 2].2424 24 The strong convergence topology is described in Sec.8.2

Lemma 7. Let ρA\,\rho_{A} be a full rank state in 𝔖⁡(ℋA)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) and {Φn}\,\{\Phi_{n}\} be a sequence of quantum operations from AA to B​CBC such that

[Φn​(ρA)]B≤ρBand[Φn​(ρA)]C≤ρC∀n[\Phi_{n}(\rho_{A})]_{B}\leq\rho_{B}\quad\textit{and}\quad[\Phi_{n}(\rho_{A})]_{C}\leq\rho_{C}\quad\forall n

for some operators ρB∈𝔗+​(ℋB)\,\rho_{B}\in\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{B}) and ρC∈𝔗+​(ℋC)\,\rho_{C}\in\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{C}). Then the sequence {Φn}\{\Phi_{n}\} is relatively compact in the strong convergence topology.

Lemma 8. Let ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC} be an arbitrary state of a tripartite system and ωA​B​Cε=(1−ε)​ωA​B​C+ε​ωA​B⊗ωC\omega^{\varepsilon}_{ABC}=(1-\varepsilon)\omega_{ABC}+\varepsilon\omega_{AB}\otimes\omega_{C}, where ε∈(0,1)\varepsilon\in(0,1), then

Proof. First assume that I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} is well defined by formula (36), i.e.

I(A:C|B)ω=H(ωA​B​C∥ωA⊗ωB​C)−H(ωA​B∥ωA⊗ωB).I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=H(\omega_{ABC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{BC})-H(\omega_{AB}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B}).

Since ωXε=ωX\omega^{\varepsilon}_{X}=\omega_{X} for X=A,B,C,A​BX=A,B,C,AB\, and ωB​Cε=(1−ε)​ωB​C+ε​ωB⊗ωC\,\omega^{\varepsilon}_{BC}=(1-\varepsilon)\omega_{BC}+\varepsilon\omega_{B}\otimes\omega_{C}, the joint convexity of the quantum relative entropy implies

I(A:C|B)ωε=H(ωεA​B​C∥ωA⊗ωεB​C)−H(ωA​B∥ωA⊗ωB)≤(1−ε)H(ωA​B​C∥ωA⊗ωB​C)+εH(ωA​B⊗ωC∥ωA⊗ωB⊗ωC)−H(ωA​B∥ωA⊗ωB)=(1−ε)I(A:C|B)ω\begin{array}[]{rl}\!I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega^{\varepsilon}}&=H(\omega^{\varepsilon}_{ABC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega^{\varepsilon}_{BC})-H(\omega_{AB}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B})\\ \\ &\leq(1-\varepsilon)H(\omega_{ABC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{BC})+\varepsilon H(\omega_{AB}\otimes\omega_{C}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B}\otimes\omega_{C})\\ \\ &-\,H(\omega_{AB}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}\otimes\omega_{B})=(1-\varepsilon)\,I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\end{array}

By using approximation property (42) it is easy to show that the inequality

I(A:C|B)ωε≤(1−ε)I(A:C|B)ω,I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega^{\varepsilon}}\leq(1-\varepsilon)\,I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega},

is valid for any state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC}. The assertion of the lemma follows from this inequality and the lower semicontinuity of I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} (Theorem 6.1). □\square

where ω~A′​B=ΦA⊗IdB​(ωA​B)\tilde{\omega}_{A^{\prime}B}=\Phi_{A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{B}(\omega_{AB}) and λ=Tr​ω~A′​B\lambda=\mathrm{Tr}\hskip 1.0pt\tilde{\omega}_{A^{\prime}B}. Since ΨA\Psi_{A} is a channel, the continuity of I​(A:B)ωI(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} on 𝒜\mathcal{A} implies, by the above remark, continuity of the left hand side of (91) on 𝒜\mathcal{A}. Since all the summands in the right hand side of (91) are lower semicontinuous functions, Lemma 2 shows that all these summands are continuous on 𝒜\mathcal{A}. □\square

Proof of Theorem 6.1. To show the uniqueness of a function with the stated properties it suffices to assume that F⁡(ω)F(\omega) is a lower semicontinuous function on the set 𝔖⁡(ℋA​B​C)\,\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC}) possessing property C3 and coinciding with I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} given by formula (36) on the set of states with finite I​(A:B)ωI(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}.

Chose any sequence of channels ΦAk:𝔗⁡(ℋA)→𝔗⁡(ℋA)\Phi_{A}^{k}:\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{A})\rightarrow\mathfrak{T}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) with finite output entropy such that limk→∞ΦAk​(ρ)=ρ\,\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\Phi_{A}^{k}(\rho)=\rho\, for any ρ∈𝔖⁡(ℋA)\,\rho\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A}). Then the lower semicontinuity of FF and property C3 imply

F(ω)=limk→∞F(ΦAk⊗IdB​C(ω))=limk→∞I(A:C|B)ΦAk⊗IdB​C​(ω),F(\omega)=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}F(\Phi_{A}^{k}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC}(\omega))=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\Phi_{A}^{k}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC}(\omega)},\quad

for any state ω∈𝔖⁡(ℋA​B​C)\omega\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC}), where I(A:C|B)ΦAk⊗IdB​C​(ω)I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\Phi_{A}^{k}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC}(\omega)} is defined by formula (36), since upper bound (19) shows that I​(A:B)ΦAk⊗IdB​C​(ω)<+∞I(A\!:\!B)_{\Phi_{A}^{k}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC}(\omega)}<+\infty for all kk. So, F⁡(ω)F(\omega) is uniquely determined.

By Remark 4.1 formulas (36), (37), (38) and (39) determine 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extensions of the quantity I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} defined in (35) respectively to the sets

𝔖1={ωA​B​C|I​(A:B)ω<+∞},𝔖2={ωA​B​C|I​(B:C)ω<+∞},𝔖3={ωA​B​C|H⁡(ωB)<+∞},𝔖4={ωA​B​C|H⁡(ωA​B​C)<+∞}.\begin{array}[]{ll}\mathfrak{S}_{1}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}<+\infty\right\},&\quad\mathfrak{S}_{2}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega}<+\infty\right\},\\ \\ \mathfrak{S}_{3}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,H(\omega_{B})<+\infty\right\},&\quad\mathfrak{S}_{4}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,H(\omega_{ABC})<+\infty\right\}.\end{array}

By uniqueness of 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension (Lemma 3) any pair of formulae (36)-(39) coincide on the set 𝔖i∩𝔖j\mathfrak{S}_{i}\cap\mathfrak{S}_{j} where both of them are well defined. So, formulae (36)-(39) correctly determine 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of the quantity I(A:C|B)I(A\!:\!C|B) defined in (35) to the set

𝔖∗=⋃i=14𝔖i={ωA​B​C|min⁡{I​(A:B)ω,I​(B:C)ω,H⁡(ωA​B​C),H⁡(ωB)}<+∞}\mathfrak{S}_{*}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{4}\mathfrak{S}_{i}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{ABC}\,|\,\min\{I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega},I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega},H(\omega_{ABC}),H(\omega_{B})\}<+\infty\right\}

of states for which at least one of these formulae is well defined. It follows, in particular, that formulae (36) and (37) coincide on the set

𝔗0={ω∈𝔗+(ℋA​B​C)|I(A:B)ω<+∞,I(B:C)ω<+∞}\mathfrak{T}_{0}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega\in\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC})\,|\,I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega}<+\infty,I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega}<+\infty\right\} (92)

containing the set 𝔗f={ω∈𝔗+(ℋA​B​C)|rankωA<+∞,rankωC<+∞}\,\mathfrak{T}_{\mathrm{f}}=\left\{\hskip 1.0pt\omega\in\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC})\,|\,\mathrm{rank}\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{A}<+\infty,\mathrm{rank}\hskip 1.0pt\omega_{C}<+\infty\right\}.

First we will prove the stated properties of Ie(A:C|B)ωI_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} for the function

F(ω)=supPA,PCI(A:C|B)Q​ω​Q,Q=PA⊗IB⊗PC,F(\omega)=\sup_{P_{A},P_{C}}I(A\!:\!C|B)_{Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega Q},\;\,Q=P_{A}\otimes I_{B}\otimes P_{C}, (93)

on the cone 𝔗+​(ℋA​B​C)\,\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC}), where

I(A:C|B)Q​ω​Q=I(A:BC)Q​ω​Q−I(A:B)Q​ω​Q=I(AB:C)Q​ω​Q−I(B:C)Q​ω​QI(A\!:\!C|B)_{Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega Q}=I(A\!:\!BC)_{Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega Q}-I(A\!:\!B)_{Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega Q}=I(AB\!:\!C)_{Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega Q}-I(B\!:\!C)_{Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega Q}

(since Q​ω​Q∈𝔗fQ\hskip 1.0pt\omega Q\in\mathfrak{T}_{\mathrm{f}}) and the supremum is over all finite rank projectors PAP_{A} in 𝔅⁡(ℋA)\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A}) and PCP_{C} in 𝔅⁡(ℋC)\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C}). Then we will show that F⁡(ω)F(\omega) coincides with the function Ie(A:C|B)ωI_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} defined by (40). By symmetry this would imply the coincidence of (40) and (41).

By Corollary 4.1 the function ω↦I(A:C|B)Q​ω​Q\,\omega\mapsto\!I(A\!:\!C|B)_{Q\hskip 1.0pt\omega Q}, Q=PA⊗IB⊗PCQ=P_{A}\otimes I_{B}\otimes P_{C}, is continuous on the cone 𝔗+​(ℋA​B​C)\,\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC}) for any finite rank projectors PAP_{A} and PCP_{C}. Hence F⁡(ω)F(\omega) is a lower semicontinuous function on 𝔗+​(ℋA​B​C)\,\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC}).

The below Lemma Appendix: Proofs of Theorems and shows, by symmetry, that the set 𝔗0\mathfrak{T}_{0} defined in (92) is invariant under local operations ΦA:A→A\Phi_{A}:A\rightarrow A and ΦC:C→C\Phi_{C}:C\rightarrow C and that

I(A:C|B)ω≥I(A:C|B)ΦA⊗IdB⊗ΦC​(ω)for anyω∈𝔗0.I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\geq I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\Phi_{\!A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{B}\otimes\Phi_{\!C}(\omega)}\quad\textrm{for any}\;\,\omega\in\mathfrak{T}_{0}. (94)

Hence

I(A:C|B)ω≥I(A:C|B)Q​ω​Qfor anyω∈𝔗0,I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\geq I(A\!:\!C|B)_{Q\omega Q}\quad\textrm{for any}\;\,\omega\in\mathfrak{T}_{0},

where Q=PA⊗IB⊗PCQ=P_{A}\otimes I_{B}\otimes P_{C}, for any finite rank projectors PAP_{A} and PCP_{C}. It follows that

F(ω)=I(A:C|B)ωfor anyω∈𝔗f,F(\omega)=I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\quad\textrm{for any}\;\,\omega\in\mathfrak{T}_{\mathrm{f}}, (95)

where I(A:C|B)ωI(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} is given by the both formulae (36) and (37).

The lower semicontinuity of FF implies

F⁡(ω)=limk→∞F⁡(Qk​ω​Qk),Qk=PAk⊗IB⊗PCk,F(\omega)=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}F(Q_{k}\omega Q_{k}),\quad Q_{k}=P^{k}_{A}\otimes I_{B}\otimes P^{k}_{C}, (96)

for arbitrary operator ω∈𝔗+​(ℋA​B​C)\omega\in\mathfrak{T}_{+}(\mathcal{H}_{ABC}) and any sequences {PAk}⊂𝔅⁡(ℋA)\{P^{k}_{A}\}\subset\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A}), {PCk}⊂𝔅⁡(ℋC)\{P^{k}_{C}\}\subset\mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C}) of finite rank projectors strongly converging to the identity operators IAI_{A}, ICI_{C}, since (93) and (95) show that

F(ω)≥I(A:C|B)Qk​ω​Qk=F(QkωQk)for allk.F(\omega)\geq I(A\!:\!C|B)_{Q_{k}\omega Q_{k}}=F(Q_{k}\omega Q_{k})\;\;\textrm{for all}\;\;k.

By definition of 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension (96) implies F(ω)=I(A:C|B)ωF(\omega)=I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} for any state ω\omega in the above-defined set 𝔖∗\mathfrak{S}_{*}.

The nonnegativity of the function FF (the first part of C1) follows from its definition (by the monotonicity of the relative entropy under partial trace).

To prove C2 note that for any state ω\omega formula (37) implies validity of C2 for all the operators Qk​ω​QkQ_{k}\omega Q_{k} in (96). So, by using faithfulness of the quantum mutual information and (96) we obtain

I​(A​B:C)ω=limk→∞I​(A​B:C)Qk​ω​Qk≥limk→∞F⁡(Qk​ω​Qk)=F⁡(ω).I(AB:C)_{\omega}=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}I(AB:C)_{Q_{k}\omega Q_{k}}\geq\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}F(Q_{k}\omega Q_{k})=F(\omega).

To prove C3 note that for any state ω\omega all the operators Qk​ω​QkQ_{k}\omega Q_{k} in (96) belong to the set 𝔗f⊂𝔗0\mathfrak{T}_{\mathrm{f}}\subset\mathfrak{T}_{0}. So, by using (94), (95), (96) and the lower semicontinuity of FF, we obtain

F⁡(ω)=limk→∞F⁡(Qk​ω​Qk)≥lim infk→∞F⁡(Ψ⁡(Qk​ω​Qk))≥F⁡(Ψ⁡(ω)),F(\omega)=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}F(Q_{k}\omega Q_{k})\geq\liminf_{k\rightarrow\infty}F(\Psi(Q_{k}\omega Q_{k}))\geq F(\Psi(\omega)),

where Ψ=ΦA⊗IdB⊗ΦC\Psi=\Phi_{A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{B}\otimes\Phi_{C}.2626 26 To simplify notation we consider quantum operations A→AA\rightarrow A and C→CC\rightarrow C. Generalization to quantum operations A→A′A\rightarrow A^{\prime} and C→C′C\rightarrow C^{\prime} is obvious.

The validity of property (10) for any state in the set 𝔖∗\mathfrak{S}_{*} follows from the existence of 𝔉\mathfrak{F}-extension of I(A:C|B)I(A\!:\!C|B) to this set and its coincidence with FF proved before. Property (42) means that

liml→∞F⁡(ωk​l)=F⁡(ωk)andlimk→∞F⁡(ωk)=F⁡(ω),\lim_{l\rightarrow\infty}F(\omega^{kl})=F(\omega^{k})\quad\textrm{and}\quad\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}F(\omega^{k})=F(\omega),

where ωk=liml→∞ωk​l\omega^{k}=\lim_{l\rightarrow\infty}\omega^{kl}. Since the state ωk\omega^{k} belong to the set 𝔖∗\mathfrak{S}_{*} for each kk, property (10) holds for this state implying the first of these limit relations. The second one follows from the lower semicontinuity of FF and property C3 proved before.

Now we can show coincidence of the function Ie(A:C|B)I_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B) defined by (40) with the function FF defined by (93).

Let Q1=PA⊗IB⊗ICQ_{1}=P_{A}\otimes I_{B}\otimes I_{C} and Q2=PA⊗IB⊗PCQ_{2}=P_{A}\otimes I_{B}\otimes P_{C}. The proved properties of the function FF imply

I(A:C|B)Q1​ω​Q1=F(Q1ωQ1)≥F(Q2ωQ2)=I(A:C|B)Q2​ω​Q2I(A\!:\!C|B)_{Q_{1}\omega Q_{1}}=F(Q_{1}\omega Q_{1})\geq F(Q_{2}\omega Q_{2})=I(A\!:\!C|B)_{Q_{2}\omega Q_{2}}

and

I(A:C|B)Q1​ω​Q1=F(Q1ωQ1)≤F(ω)I(A\!:\!C|B)_{Q_{1}\omega Q_{1}}=F(Q_{1}\omega Q_{1})\leq F(\omega)

for any state ω\omega. The first of these inequalities implies Ie(A:C|B)ω≥F(ω)I_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\geq F(\omega), while the second one shows that Ie(A:C|B)ω≤F(ω)I_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\leq F(\omega).

Properties C4-C5 of Ie(A:C|B)ωI_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} can be derived by approximation from the same properties of the conditional mutual information in the finite-dimensional settings. In the case of C4 it suffices to use property (42). In the case of C5 the second part of Corollary 6.1 (i.e. property (45)) is necessary.2727 27 Property C5 of Ie(A:C|B)ωI_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega} is not used in the proof of Corollary 6.1.

To prove the second part of C1 note that Ie(A:C|B)ω=0I_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}=0 implies, by Proposition 8.4 in Sect.8.4. (proved independently), the existence of a channel Φ:B→B​C\Phi:B\rightarrow BC such that ωA​B​C=IdA⊗Φ⁡(ωA​B)\,\omega_{ABC}=\mathrm{Id}_{A}\otimes\Phi(\omega_{AB}). The converse statement follows from definition (40) of Ie(A:C|B)ωI_{\mathrm{e}}(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}. □\square

Lemma 9. For arbitrary quantum operation ΦA:A→A\,\Phi_{A}:A\rightarrow A the set 𝔗0\,\mathfrak{T}_{0} is invariant under the map ΦA⊗IdB​C\,\Phi_{\!A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC} and I(A:C|B)ω≥I(A:C|B)ΦA⊗IdB​C​(ω)\,I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\omega}\geq I(A\!:\!C|B)_{\Phi_{\!A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC}(\omega)} for any ω∈𝔗0\,\omega\in\mathfrak{T}_{0}.

Proof. If ΦA\hskip 1.0pt\Phi_{A} is a channel then the assertion of the lemma directly follows from monotonicity of the quantum mutual information and formula (37), since in this case I​(B:C)ΦA⊗IdB​C​(ω)=I​(B:C)ωI(B\!:\!C)_{\Phi_{\!A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC}(\omega)}=I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega} for any state ωA​B​C\omega_{ABC}.

If ΦA\hskip 1.0pt\Phi_{A} is a trace non-preserving operation then consider the channel ΨA=ΦA⊕Δ\Psi_{A}=\Phi_{A}\oplus\Delta from AA to A′=A⊕AcA^{\prime}=A\oplus A^{\mathrm{c}}, where Δ⁡(ρ)=[Tr​ρ−Tr​ΦA​(ρ)]​σ\Delta(\rho)=[\mathrm{Tr}\rho-\mathrm{Tr}\Phi_{A}(\rho)]\sigma is a quantum operation from AA to AcA^{\mathrm{c}} determined by a fixed state σ∈𝔖⁡(ℋAc)\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}(\mathcal{H}_{A^{\mathrm{c}}}).

Let ω~A​B​C=ΦA⊗IdB​C​(ωA​B​C)\tilde{\omega}_{ABC}=\Phi_{A}\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC}(\omega_{ABC}), ωA​B​Cc=Δ⊗IdB​C​(ωA​B​C)\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{ABC}=\Delta\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{BC}(\omega_{ABC}) and λ=Tr​ω~A​B​C\lambda=\mathrm{Tr}\hskip 1.0pt\tilde{\omega}_{ABC}. To prove the invariance of 𝔗0\,\mathfrak{T}_{0} it suffices to note that I​(A:B)ω~≤I​(A:B)ωI(A\!:\!B)_{\tilde{\omega}}\leq I(A\!:\!B)_{\omega} by monotonicity of the quantum mutual information and that inequality (87) implies I​(B:C)ω~≤I​(B:C)ω~+ωc+h2​(λ)=I​(B:C)ω+h2​(λ)I(B\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}}\leq I(B\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}+\omega^{\mathrm{c}}}+h_{2}(\lambda)=I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega}+h_{2}(\lambda) (the last equality holds, since ΨA\Psi_{A} is a channel).

Similarly to (91) we have

I(A′B:C)ω~+ωc=I(AB:C)ω~+H(ω~C∥λωC)+H(ωA​B​Cc∥ωA​Bc⊗ωC),I(A^{\prime}B\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}+\omega^{\mathrm{c}}}=I(AB\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}}+H\left(\tilde{\omega}_{C}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\lambda\omega_{C}\right)+H\left(\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{ABC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{AB}\otimes\omega_{C}\right), (97)

while the joint convexity of the relative entropy and relation (8) imply

I​(B:C)ω~+ωc=H(ω~B​C+ωcB​C∥(ω~B+ωcB)⊗ωC)≤H(ω~B​C∥ω~B⊗ωC)+H(ωcB​C∥ωcB⊗ωC)=I(B:C)ω~+H(ω~C∥λωC)+H(ωcB​C∥ωcB⊗ωC).\begin{array}[]{rl}I(B\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}+\omega^{\mathrm{c}}}&=\,H\left(\tilde{\omega}_{BC}+\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{BC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt(\tilde{\omega}_{B}+\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{B})\otimes\omega_{C}\right)\\ \\ &\leq\,H\left(\tilde{\omega}_{BC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\tilde{\omega}_{B}\otimes\omega_{C}\right)+H\left(\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{BC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{B}\otimes\omega_{C}\right)\\ \\ &=\,I(B\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}}+H\left(\tilde{\omega}_{C}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\lambda\omega_{C}\right)+H\left(\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{BC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{B}\otimes\omega_{C}\right).\end{array} (98)

We have I​(A′​B:C)ω~+ωc≤I​(A​B:C)ωI(A^{\prime}B\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}+\omega^{\mathrm{c}}}\leq I(AB\!:\!C)_{\omega} and I​(B:C)ω~+ωc=I​(B:C)ωI(B\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}+\omega^{\mathrm{c}}}=I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega} (since ΨA\Psi_{A} is a channel). Hence it follows from (97) and (98) that

I​(A​B:C)ω~−I​(B:C)ω~≤I​(A​B:C)ω−I​(B:C)ω−δI(AB\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}}-I(B\!:\!C)_{\tilde{\omega}}\leq I(AB\!:\!C)_{\omega}-I(B\!:\!C)_{\omega}-\delta

where δ=H(ωA​B​Cc∥ωA​Bc⊗ωC)−H(ωB​Cc∥ωBc⊗ωC)≥0\,\delta=H\left(\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{ABC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{AB}\otimes\omega_{C}\right)-H\left(\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{BC}\hskip 1.0pt\|\hskip 1.0pt\omega^{\mathrm{c}}_{B}\otimes\omega_{C}\right)\geq 0\, by monotonicity of the relative entropy. □\square
